sharyn.name: Charyn Canyon
sharyn.lead: One of the most beautiful places in Kazakhstan — locals call it the "valley of fortified castles."
sharyn.bodyHtml:
Charyn Canyon lies 195 km from the city of Almaty. It is 200 km long, and its rock formations rise from 150 to 300 meters. The "Valley of Towers," which is especially popular with tourists, is 2 km long and 20–80 m wide.

Charyn is often compared to America's Grand Canyon and called its little brother. Huge rocks that seem to touch the sky resemble a fairy-tale city that built itself: their shapes look strikingly like man-made buildings and towers.

Images of wild animals show that birds and animals lived in this area as far back as the Paleolithic. Barberry and turanga poplar grow in the lower part of the canyon.

kolsai.name: Kolsai Lakes
kolsai.lead: A chain of three lakes in the Northern Tien Shan: Lower, Middle and Upper Kolsai.
kolsai.bodyHtml:
The Kolsai Lakes are a system of three lakes in the Northern Tien Shan, which links the Kungei Alatau and Trans-Ili Alatau ranges. They lie one after another at different altitudes along the Kolsai River.

Upper Kolsai lies 2,650 m above sea level, Middle Kolsai at 2,280 m and Lower Kolsai at 1,800 m. The lower lake is 1,520 m long and 222 m wide on average.

The neighboring Lake Kaindy was formed by a powerful earthquake in 1911: water flooded the valley, and the trees ended up underwater. Because the lake water stays at around +6°C even in summer, the needles on the trees have survived to this day.

khantengri.name: Khan Tengri
khantengri.lead: The most beautiful peak of the Tien Shan, which Kazakhs call "Aspantau" — it stands where the borders of Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and China meet.
khantengri.bodyHtml:
Khan Tengri is one of the high peaks of the Tien Shan, which Kazakhs call "Aspantau." Its southeastern side belongs to Kazakhstan, its eastern side to China and its western side to Kyrgyzstan.

Rising to more than 7,000 meters, it is counted among the most beautiful peaks in the world. Until 1960, local people called it Khantengir.

The marble walls of this sharp, four-sided pyramid catch the eye from far away. Climbers reach the summit via the South and North Inylchek glaciers.

muztau.name: Belukha
muztau.fact: Highest peak of the Altai · 4,506 m
muztau.lead: The highest glacier-capped peak of the Altai Mountains in Russia and Kazakhstan. Kazakhs called it Aksumbi and Aktaiky.
muztau.bodyHtml:
Belukha (Muztau in Kazakh) is the highest glacier-capped peak of the Altai Mountains in Russia and Kazakhstan (4,506 m). It rises on the eastern side of the Katun Range, near the border between Kazakhstan and the Altai region.

Near its summit lie the Greater and Lesser Berel and Mensu glaciers, which give rise to the Katun River. The river basins connected with Belukha contain 162 glaciers covering 146 square kilometers.

The people of Altai affectionately call Belukha "the abode of God" and "the Great Elder." Perhaps it got these names because it is covered in eternal snow from top to bottom.

alakol.name: Lake Alakol
alakol.lead: A closed lake rich in iodine and salts, known for its healing properties. Silk Road caravans once passed along its shores.
alakol.bodyHtml:
Alakol is a closed lake with no outflow, located in Almaty and East Kazakhstan regions. More than 15 rivers flow into it.

Its water is rich in minerals, iodine and salt, and its health benefits have been medically proven. Travelers on the Silk Road are said to have rested on its shores and drawn strength from its waters.

Between the 12th and 19th centuries, the lake was known by several names: Turge-Nor, Alaktagol and Alateniz.

okzhetpes.name: Okzhetpes
okzhetpes.lead: A granite rock rising above the clear waters of Lake Auliekol. Shokan Ualikhanov collected more than 15 legends about it.
okzhetpes.bodyHtml:
Okzhetpes stands next to Mount Kokshe, the highest point of the Kokshetau Upland. It is made of granite, with steep slopes where pine and birch grow.

Many legends are told about this rock above the clear waters of Lake Auliekol. Shokan Ualikhanov collected more than 15 legends and tales, and Saken Seifullin told the story of Okzhetpes in his poem "Kokshetau."

korgalzhyn.name: Korgalzhyn Nature Reserve
korgalzhyn.lead: Around 60 lakes that are home to millions of birds. Three of the world's 8 bird migration routes pass through Lake Tengiz.
korgalzhyn.bodyHtml:
Korgalzhyn Nature Reserve lies 120 km southwest of the city of Astana. In 1968, it was re-established as a nature reserve by government decree. It covers 258,963 hectares.

There are 8 bird migration routes in the world, and three of them cross Lake Tengiz in this reserve. That is why millions of birds live on Korgalzhyn's nearly 70 lakes.

The reserve belongs to Group "A" under the Ramsar Convention, and in 2007 its lakes were designated an Important Bird Area (IBA) of international significance.

tanbaly.name: Tamgaly Petroglyphs
tanbaly.lead: One of the oldest monuments of Zhetysu — thousands of images carved into the rock since the Bronze Age.
tanbaly.bodyHtml:
This archaeological complex lies in the southeastern part of the Chu-Ili Mountains in Almaty Region, 170 km northwest of Almaty.

The Tamgaly complex includes more than 5,000 petroglyphs from different historical periods, as well as settlements, burial grounds and sacrificial sites. Its most valuable part is the petroglyphs of the Middle Bronze Age.

Researchers particularly highlight the high aesthetic value and spiritual impact of the Tamgaly petroglyphs.

yassawi.name: Mausoleum of Khoja Ahmed Yasawi
yassawi.lead: A jewel of medieval architecture in Turkistan and the spiritual center of the Turkic world.
yassawi.bodyHtml:
The Mausoleum of Khoja Ahmed Yasawi is a jewel of medieval architecture in Turkistan. It was built at the end of the 14th century by order of Amir Timur over the grave of the great thinker Khoja Ahmed Yasawi.

In 2003, the mausoleum was added to the UNESCO World Heritage List. For centuries, this towering building with its blue dome has been a sacred place of pilgrimage for the peoples of Central Asia.

otyrar.name: Ancient city of Otrar
otyrar.lead: A major center of trade and learning on the Silk Road, and the capital of the region where the great thinker al-Farabi was born.
otyrar.bodyHtml:
The ancient city of Otrar lies 7 km northwest of Shauildir, the center of Otrar District. In history it is also known as Turarband, Tarband and Farab.

The city was an important center on the trade route linking Iran and Central Asia with Siberia, Mongolia and China. Otrar was the capital of the region where Abu Nasr al-Farabi was born.

beket.name: Beket Ata Mosque
beket.lead: The most sacred pilgrimage site in Mangystau — an underground mosque carved into the rock by Beket Ata.
beket.bodyHtml:
Beket Myrzagululy (1750–1813) was a prominent Kazakh religious figure, educator and warrior. A master builder, he carved underground mosques in the Mangystau, Atyrau and Ustyurt areas, where children were taught.

In the underground mosque at Ogylandy, he founded a Sufi school. Today the place is known as a sacred site that gives people spiritual nourishment and shows the way to those who have lost it.

ulytau.name: Ulytau
ulytau.fact: The heart of the Kazakh land
ulytau.lead: The highest point of western Saryarka. A land where khans were raised on white felt, and which Asan Kaigy called Zheruiyk (the promised land).
ulytau.bodyHtml:
Ulytau covers the southeast of the Turgai Trough and the northern part of Betpak-Dala. It is not only the highest point of western Saryarka, but also its "heart" and the "center of the world."

It was here that the Kazakhs raised their sultans on white felt and proclaimed them khans. Jochi Khan, Alasha Khan and Tokhtamysh Khan, as well as the warrior Edige, are buried here. Asan Kaigy called this land Zheruiyk, a promised land where the Kazakh people could live well.

zhidebai.name: Zhidebai-Borili
zhidebai.lead: A historical and cultural complex that gives a full picture of Abai's life and work.
zhidebai.bodyHtml:
The complex is located in the settlement of Zhidebai in Abai District. Abai's winter home, inherited from Kunanbai in 1884, was turned into a house museum.

The items in the museum's five rooms and three halls were collected from the poet's relatives, friends and contemporaries. The outside of the house still looks as it did in Abai's time.

baiterek.name: Baiterek
baiterek.lead: A symbol of the independent country: its height of 97 meters stands for 1997, when the capital moved to Astana.
baiterek.bodyHtml:
The Baiterek monument in the center of Astana is a symbol of the independent Kazakh state and of its people's revival and renewal. The structure rises to 97 meters, a reference to 1997, the year the new capital was proclaimed.

The main idea behind the monument is the World Tree. The "Bata" (Blessing) composition at the top holds the blessings of the leaders of world religions who gathered in Astana in 2003.

berel.name: Berel Kurgans
berel.fact: More than 70 burial mounds · Saka period
berel.lead: A famous Saka and Turkic burial ground where permafrost has kept clothing, horse gear and wooden objects from decaying.
berel.bodyHtml:
The Berel burial ground lies 7–8 km southwest of the village of Berel in Katon-Karagay District. The earliest mounds date back to the 4th–3rd centuries BC, and the later ones to the ancient Turkic period.

Thanks to the permafrost inside the large mounds, clothing, horse harnesses, wooden objects and items made of leather and felt have been well preserved. The site was studied by V. Radlov in 1865, and Z. Samashev has been researching it since 1998.

bayanaul.name: Konyr Aulie Cave
bayanaul.lead: A sacred place where people have come to make wishes since ancient times. Mashhur Zhusup called it "the place where saints ask Allah for His decree."
bayanaul.bodyHtml:
This sacred cave in the Bayanaul Mountains lies three kilometers from Lake Zhasybay. Known as Konyr Aulie or the Aulie Tas cave, it has long been regarded as the blessed heart of Bayanaul.

Water constantly collects in a cauldron-like hollow deep inside the cave; it is considered sacred and healing for the sick. Mashhur Zhusup praised the sanctity of this place and called it "the place where saints ask Allah for His decree."

tamshybulak.name: Tamshybulak
tamshybulak.lead: A healing spring that breaks through stone walls and flows drop by drop. Shokan Ualikhanov studied it in 1859–1865.
tamshybulak.bodyHtml:
Tamshybulak is in the center of the village of Kapal in Aksu District. Breaking through ancient stone walls and gathering drop by drop, the spring does not freeze even in winter.

Since ancient times, local people have used its water to treat various illnesses. The first written records of Tamshybulak were made by Shokan Ualikhanov.

esik.name: Esik Kurgans
esik.lead: A burial ground of Saka kings where the "Golden Man," one of the symbols of independent Kazakhstan, was found in 1969.
esik.bodyHtml:
The Esik Kurgans are a burial ground of Saka kings at the foot of the Trans-Ili Alatau. In 1969, the remains of a warrior in golden clothing — the famous "Golden Man" — were found in one of the mounds here.

Today the "Golden Man" stands atop Kazakhstan's Independence Monument, and an open-air museum operates near the kurgans.

buryngy-musylman-mektebi.name: Former Muslim School
buryngy-musylman-mektebi.fact: The monument represents provincial building, which is one of the peculiar examples of wooden architecture of the late…
buryngy-musylman-mektebi.lead: The monument represents provincial building, which is one of the peculiar examples of wooden architecture of the late 19th and early 20th century. It is a dwelling house in the form of a wooden framework, imitating a Russian house.
buryngy-musylman-mektebi.bodyHtml:
The monument represents provincial building, which is one of the peculiar examples of wooden architecture of the late 19th and early 20th century.

It is a dwelling house in the form of a wooden framework, imitating a Russian house. The affluent carved wooden decor harmoniously decorates the plat bands, valance, curtain rodsand the central part of the carved gable with a paired decorative dormer. All these elements belong to the pseudo-Russian style in the architecture of the end of the 19th century and were calledas the "cock" style.
The building is a monument of the republican protection category.

It was built by the Akmola merchant StepanBelov.Later, the merchant sold the building to the Tatar-Muslim community.

The further history of the monument is related to education. In early 20th centurythe first Muslim school of Akmola for girls situated here. Since 1907 the Kyrgyz-Tatar elementary school began to work in this building, where 27 pupils were taught.

During the Soviet period, the school was reorganized into 7-year-old Kazakh school number 4, and girls were also taught there. In 1912 the founder of modern Kazakh literature, poet and writer Saken Seifullin taught in this school.

Separated teaching method was existed in the Soviet Union until 1954. So in 1954, the united schoolfor boys and girls was resited to a new building.
And the building of the former school in the early sixties was inherited to the kindergarten "Belochka", which was located here for almost 30 years - until the mid-1990s.

In 1996, the building was transmitted to the Kazakh musical and drama theater named after KalybekKuanyshbaev and was used as an art and production workshop for making props.
It may safely be said that this building is a great treasure for every Kazakhstani, because it is connected with the history of education, and also with the name of the outstanding Kazakh poet, writer and public figure Saken Seifullin.

At the present time, the State Public Utility Enterprise "The department of Historical and cultural heritage of saving secrets and objects" of Nur-Sultan City is located here.

asharshylyq-qurbandaryna-eskertkish-monu.name: Monument to the Holodomor victims of 1932-1933
asharshylyq-qurbandaryna-eskertkish-monu.fact: Located in the old historical part of the city, in one of the main tourist centers of the capital - at the…
asharshylyq-qurbandaryna-eskertkish-monu.lead: Located in the old historical part of the city, in one of the main tourist centers of the capital - at the intersection of the Republic Avenue and Abay Street. Nearby are the palace "Zhastar", "Abay" and "Intercontinental" hotels, a post office, and the city department is also nearby.
asharshylyq-qurbandaryna-eskertkish-monu.bodyHtml:
Located in the old historical part of the city, in one of the main tourist centers of the capital - at the intersection of the Republic Avenue and Abay Street. Nearby are the palace "Zhastar", "Abay" and "Intercontinental" hotels, a post office, and the city department is also nearby. The monument is well seen from the main points of the surrounding space.

The monument is dedicated to the innocent victims of the Starvation in Kazakhstan in 1932-1933. This is the greatest tragedy of Kazakh people, which claimed the lives of 2 million 400 thousand people.

The sculptural composition of the monument consists of three parts.

The dominant part of the monument - the image of a woman-mother, by will, desire and pleas, she, as it soars above the surface of the earth. With despair and hope, she turns to heaven for help in maintaining and procreating. To enhance the perception of this image, the sculpture is somewhat hypertrophied and executed in an impulsive manner of modeling.

On either side of the main axis of the composition are figures that occupy in their embodiment an intermediate position between the realistic and conventional image adopted in tombstones installed on the burial places of Kazakhs.

By such a decision, the author emphasizes the connection of the departed tribesmen who have gone to another world. And as the basis of everything - the figure of a boy, realistically alive, but left in indecision and confusion. For him - the symbol of the continuation of life and the family - reading is offered, in memory of the victims of the famine of 1932-1933.

The background of the sculptural composition "Wall of Sorrow" is represented by a height of 5 meters and an arc length of 21 meters.

Taking into account the location and significance of the monument, high-quality bronze and granite are used to create the sculpture and architectural part of the monument.

To enhance the expressiveness of the monument, night illumination is used.

konstantin-elena-shirkeui.name: Saints Constantine and Helen Orthodox Cathedral
konstantin-elena-shirkeui.fact: The Konstantin-Elena Church is located on the Republic Avenue.
konstantin-elena-shirkeui.lead: The Konstantin-Elena Church is located on the Republic Avenue. The church is one-table in plan, five-domed, designed in the form of a regular cross. The length of the building is 33 meters, width - 8 meters. Two outstanding extensions on the sides, which give the church a cross look, have dimensions of 3.6x4 meters.
konstantin-elena-shirkeui.bodyHtml:
The Konstantin-Elena Church is located on the Republic Avenue.

The church is one-table in plan, five-domed, designed in the form of a regular cross. The length of the building is 33 meters, width - 8 meters. Two outstanding extensions on the sides, which give the church a cross look, have dimensions of 3.6x4 meters. Strict and, at the same time, graceful lines of the contours of the Orthodox church are directed upwards, giving the building airy lightness and elegance.

Above the cubic volume stands an eight-faceted drum with windows, covered with a shallow tent, completed by the command post. Above the vestibule, a bell tower with a rectangular base, an 8-drum drum and, in the upper part, belfry spans, overlapping also with a gentle tent with the same head as the central tent, rises. The bell tower is located above the western entrance to the building.

Now it is plastered and gives the impression of stone.
The monument is of value, as the only cult building in the city that has survived since the 19th century, and reflects the development of the city's culture at a certain stage in the history of urban development.

The history of the monument begins on September 12, 1849, when the priest of the field camp of Akmola church, Mikhail Nikolsky, asked the border guard to start construction of the church from the early spring of 1850. The project and estimates for the construction of the wooden church were developed by June 1850.

July 8, 1856, the Cathedral Archpriest John Toropov consecrated the church in the name of the Holy Equal-to-the-Apostles kings Constantine and Helena. The first priest of the church was the priest Michael Nikolsky. The final work on the exterior decoration of the temple ended in the summer of 1858.

By a decree of April 27, 1893, the Tobolsk Spiritual Consistory authorized, at the request of the Akmola Cossacks, the transfer of the Constantine-Elenin Church to Akmola page to the square. The laying on the page square was carried out on May 14, 1900. The transfer process was completed by the beginning of 1902.

As before, the temple was arranged in a one-table plan, in the form of a regular cross, but significant changes also appeared: the church became five-domed. This corresponded to the official direction of architecture of those years.

In 1938, the Konstantin-Yelenin Church was closed. Crosses and bells were removed, the bell tower was dismantled. In 1940 the building was transferred to the Museum of Local History and History. During the Great Patriotic War in 1941-1942, the building of the church housed a separate battalion of communications of the 29th Infantry Division, which was being formed in Akmolinsk. In 1942, according to numerous requests of the faithful, Akmolinsk was allowed to resume worship in the Constantine-Elenin Church.

From this time until today, worship services are held in one of the oldest buildings of the iconic architecture.

qazaq-eli-monumenti.name: "Kazakh Yeli" Monument
qazaq-eli-monumenti.fact: The memorial complex "Kazakh country" is the first monumental monument in history dedicated to the historical destiny…
qazaq-eli-monumenti.lead: The memorial complex "Kazakh country" is the first monumental monument in history dedicated to the historical destiny of Kazakhs. The opening took place on the day of the 10th anniversary of the capital - July 6, 2008 - with the participation of the Head of State Nursultan Nazarbayev.
qazaq-eli-monumenti.bodyHtml:
The memorial complex "Kazakh country" is the first monumental monument in history dedicated to the historical destiny of Kazakhs.

The opening took place on the day of the 10th anniversary of the capital - July 6, 2008 - with the participation of the Head of State Nursultan Nazarbayev.

It represents a stele with birds Samruk installed on its top and four bronze bas-reliefs at the base: "The First President and the people of Kazakhstan", "Courage", "Creation" and "Future".

The total area of the monument is 5 hectares, the area of the adjacent territory is 11 hectares.

The authors of the monument are the architect Samatbek Bokebay and the artist Sembigali Smagulov.

The height of the monument is 91 meters, which symbolizes 1991, when Kazakhstan became an independent state. The marble foundation of the monument represents purity of thoughts and interethnic harmony of the people of Kazakhstan. Stela, looking upwards, on top of which the sacred bird Samruk is installed, demonstrates the desire of the people of Kazakhstan for further development and prosperity.

It is symbolic that the authors decided to create a multi-figure sculptural ensemble, which is divided into four bas-reliefs. Each of them initially has its own meaning and idea and aims to show different facets and phenomena of the history of the country. For example, in the complex "Heroes" - "Courage" - the images of ancient soldiers and modern defenders of the Fatherland symbolize the heroic episodes of the country's development.

One of the bright elements of the ensemble is the composition "The First President and the People", where the First President of the Republic, as a symbol of Kazakhstan's independence, swears an oath of loyalty to the people and the country. In the central part of the composition "Zhasampazdyk" - "Creation" - the main is the image of the Man-creator - in the person of a metallurgist and oilman, an engineer and a grain grower, a builder and an astronaut.

The future of the country is brightly reflected in the monument. The composition theme of the bas-relief "Bolashak" - "Future" - demonstrates the spirit of the youth, the desire to achieve the Kazakhstan dream.

Unexpected decision of architects can be considered the construction in another part of the bas-relief "Bolash" - "Future" - a pair figure of the newlyweds. After all, it is not so often possible to meet monuments or monuments, where there is an appeal to the value of marriage and family. Next to them are figures of young people who symbolize not only youth, optimism, the desire for a new, but also the fact that the entire nation is young and growing, and hence - ambitious. It is no coincidence, as historians note, that the eighteenth year in the history of sovereign Kazakhstan is another milestone on the way to achieving new and grandiose heights.

On the square near the monument "Kazakh Eli" are located one of the main objects of public and cultural life of the country: the Palace of Independence, the Palace of Creativity "Shabyt", the Mosque "Khazret Sultan", the Palace of Peace and Harmony.

ahmet-baitursynuly-muzei-uii.name: Museum-House of Akhmet Baytursynuly
ahmet-baitursynuly-muzei-uii.fact: The cultural and scientific address dedicated to the life and career of Akhmet Baitursynov is located at the junction…
ahmet-baitursynuly-muzei-uii.lead: The cultural and scientific address dedicated to the life and career of Akhmet Baitursynov is located at the junction of A. Baitursynov and Zhambyl streets in Almaty. The house where A. Baitursynov lived from 1934 to 1937 was officially opened as a museum in 1998 on the eve of the 125th anniversary of the poet.
ahmet-baitursynuly-muzei-uii.bodyHtml:
The cultural and scientific address dedicated to the life and career of Akhmet Baitursynov is located at the junction of A. Baitursynov and Zhambyl streets in Almaty. The house where A. Baitursynov lived from 1934 to 1937 was officially opened as a museum in 1998 on the eve of the 125th anniversary of the poet. The museum consists of a 1.5 floor building. It has four rooms and a basement. Basement - office of museum staff. Three rooms - an exhibition hall, one room - an auditorium. On the scientist's birthday, September 5, the traditional Akhmet studies “Bow to the person” are held annually.

A. Baitursynov (1873-1938) - alash leader, poet, great linguist, literary researcher, turkologist, publicist, teacher, translator, public figure. He was arrested in October 1937 and shot in February 1938 after several months of investigation. The prisoner answered the questions of investigators as follows: “My dream is to raise the wealth and culture of the Kazakh people to the highest possible level. Since that good deed is just beginning, I have the power to satisfy only my desires”.

In the yard of the museum there is a bust of the teacher of the nation A. Baitursynov.

Reference: The Kazakhstan sacred objects
of whole national importance. – Astana: Foliant, 2017.–407-409-pp.; Sacred Kazakhstan. 1-volume. – Almaty: “Arys” edition, 2017. –177-p.

raiymbek-batyr-kesenesi.name: Mausoleum of Rayimbek Batyr
raiymbek-batyr-kesenesi.fact: The mausoleum of the hero is located on Raiymbek Batyr Avenue in Almaty. Raimbek Tukeeuly (1705-1785) - hero, commander.
raiymbek-batyr-kesenesi.lead: The mausoleum of the hero is located on Raiymbek Batyr Avenue in Almaty. Raimbek Tukeeuly (1705-1785) - hero, commander. Raimbek Batyr not only demonstrated the courage in the fight against the Dzungar invaders, but also served as an ambassador. He reached effective deals with foresight and became a modern politician.
raiymbek-batyr-kesenesi.bodyHtml:
The mausoleum of the hero is located on Raiymbek Batyr Avenue in Almaty. Raimbek Tukeeuly (1705-1785) - hero, commander. Raimbek Batyr not only demonstrated the courage in the fight against the Dzungar invaders, but also served as an ambassador. He reached effective deals with foresight and became a modern politician.

In 1733, he went to Dzungaria as an ambassador with Bolek Batyr. Defeating Kalmykia's noyan batyrs Badam, Koryn, Aganas, Seker, etc. and khans, he was one of the leaders in the liberation of the Karatau region and Semirechye from the enemy. Raimbek Batyr is a man who was called a “seer” and “saint” during his lifetime.

Before his death, Raimbek Batyr said to his descendants: “Put my body on a white camel and let go of my head. He told to bury him wherever he fell. “The place where the white camel landed is current Raimbek Batyr Avenue in Almaty.

Reference: The Kazakhstan sacred objects
of whole national importance. – Astana: Foliant, 2017. –318-321-pp.

bespaqyr-kesenesi.name: The Mausoleum of Bespakyr
bespaqyr-kesenesi.fact: Bespakyr mausoleum is a unique religious monument of Kazakhstan, built in the 30s of the XIX century.
bespaqyr-kesenesi.lead: Bespakyr mausoleum is a unique religious monument of Kazakhstan, built in the 30s of the XIX century. It is located in Korgalzhyn district of Akmola region.
bespaqyr-kesenesi.bodyHtml:
Bespakyr mausoleum is a unique religious monument of Kazakhstan, built in the 30s of the XIX century. It is located in Korgalzhyn district of Akmola region.

According to the legend, the mazar was built in honor of five heroes who fought in the national liberation uprising led by Kenesary Kasymuly in the 30s of the XIX century. That is why it is called Bespakyr. The construction of the two-room mazar is different. Through the door on the east side, you can enter an oval room about three meters in size. The door is curved, high, arched and decorated with recesses. The height of the walls is about three meters. According to sources, the raw bricks used for the mausoleum were originally made of sheep's milk mixed with horsehair and clay. Horse hair is strong and durable, which does not wear out over the years. The fact that the yen does not rot from the wind, snow and rain in the steppe, and does not turn into mud again, shows that the masters who make bricks are skilled professionals. The round tomb consists of a domed spherical burial chamber and a portal with a conical dome. The mausoleum describes a different type of mausoleum in the form of a dome, a sagana.

.

Reference: The Kazakhstan sacred objects
of whole national importance. – Astana: Foliant, 2017.– 379-380-pp.; Sacred Kazakhstan. 1-volume. – Almaty: “Arys” edition, 2017. –82-p.

bytygai-kesenesi.name: Bytygay Mausoleum
bytygai-kesenesi.fact: It is located in Korgalzhyn district of Akmola region in 2 km east of the village of Korgalzhyn, on the left bank of…
bytygai-kesenesi.lead: It is located in Korgalzhyn district of Akmola region in 2 km east of the village of Korgalzhyn, on the left bank of the river Nura. Botogay mausoleum (other names Bytygai, Tatagai) is an architectural monument of the XI-XII centuries. Botogay is a medieval portal - a domed mausoleum.
bytygai-kesenesi.bodyHtml:
It is located in Korgalzhyn district of Akmola region in 2 km east of the village of Korgalzhyn, on the left bank of the river Nura. Botogay mausoleum (other names Bytygai, Tatagai) is an architectural monument of the XI-XII centuries.

Botogay is a medieval portal - a domed mausoleum. The only medieval mausoleum in Kazakhstan, measured and described in 1831-1856. The Botogay mausoleum was painted in 1862 by ethnographer and scientist Chokan Valikhanov. Many caravan routes along the Great Silk Road met here.

Botagay was first mapped in Russia in 1694. It was painted for Tauke khan by Russian ambassadors F. Skibin and M. Troshin. In 1762, the book “The work of Peter Rychkov, a collegiate adviser to the Imperial Academy of Sciences” was published in St. Petersburg. The Russian scientist gives the following information about Bytygai: “Bytygai is the site of a great city in the Kyrgyz-Kaisak horde on the Nura River, which flows into Lake Korgalzhyn. By its characteristics, the city is located ten kilometers away, and the size of the square buildings in the form of a palace is so large that it is about three hundred square meters. There is a mosque here and many ruined stone buildings. " After the death of Tauke Khan, Bytygai was deserted and almost destroyed.

In 1816, I.P. Shangin inspected the mausoleum, gave a brief description, outlined the plan of the building and the front of the mausoleum. In 1825, adviser Demidov wrote about this monument in a letter to Alexander I about the transfer of the Siberian and Orenburg borders to Kazakhstan.

Reference: Kazakhstan sacred objects
of whole national importance. – Astana: Foliant, 2017. –198-200 pp.

olzhabai-tolebaiuly-mazary.name: Mausoleum of Olzhabay Tolebayuly
olzhabai-tolebaiuly-mazary.fact: The mausoleum of Olzhabay batyr is located near Olzhabay village of Ereymentau district of Akmola region.
olzhabai-tolebaiuly-mazary.lead: The mausoleum of Olzhabay batyr is located near Olzhabay village of Ereymentau district of Akmola region. Olzhabay Tolebayevich (1709–1785) was a flag bearer of Abylai Khan, a hero in the war against the Dzungars and China. He studied at the Turkestan madrasah and was fluent in Arabic and Kalmyk.
olzhabai-tolebaiuly-mazary.bodyHtml:
The mausoleum of Olzhabay batyr is located near Olzhabay village of Ereymentau district of Akmola region. Olzhabay Tolebayevich (1709–1785) was a flag bearer of Abylai Khan, a hero in the war against the Dzungars and China.

He studied at the Turkestan madrasah and was fluent in Arabic and Kalmyk. According to the memoirs of academician A. Margulan, in 1762, together with Olzhabay's nephew Edige, Catherine II wrote a letter asking for a pasture. The period of Olzhabay Batyr's life was a difficult time in the history of the Kazakh people, which was called "Aktaban shubyryndy, Alkakol sulama". He helped to save Ablai, who fell into the hands of the Dzungars, supported the policy of centralization of the state and made a significant contribution to it. Olzhabay took part in the liberation of Turkestan and Tashkent from the Dzungars in 1735, in the battles that liberated Bayanaul from Kaldan Seren in 1736, and in 1756 defeated the Chinese army that invaded the Kazakh lands. The highlight of his heroism was the battle with the Kalmyks on the slopes of Bayanaul.

Satisfied with his heroism in battles, the khan of the Middle Zhuz Abilmambet presented him with a sword with a golden handle. Olzhabay Tolybayevich, who studied at a Turkestan madrasah and learned Arabic, was fluent in Kalmyk. His knowledge of the language also helped him to go to the release of Ablai Khan and take part in negotiations.

Reference: Kazakhstan sacred objects
of whole national importance. – Astana: Foliant, 2017. –323-325-pp.

uali-han-kesenesi.name: Mausoleum of Uali Khan
uali-han-kesenesi.fact: Uali khan (1781-1821) was the khan of the Middle Zhuz.
uali-han-kesenesi.lead: Uali khan (1781-1821) was the khan of the Middle Zhuz. From an early age he came to power and took part in the campaigns of Abylai Khan in Dzungaria and Central Asia. In 1769, he leaded the Kazakh embassy in China.
uali-han-kesenesi.bodyHtml:
Uali khan (1781-1821) was the khan of the Middle Zhuz. From an early age he came to power and took part in the campaigns of Abylai Khan in Dzungaria and Central Asia. In 1769, he leaded the Kazakh embassy in China. After the death of his father Abylai khan in 1781, at the will of Abylai khan, the people's assembly elected his eldest son Uali as the new khan of the Middle Zhuz. Uali Khan announced his appointment to St. Petersburg and Beijing and asked the Russian and Chinese governments to recognize him as the khan of the Middle Zhuz. In 1781, Russia and China recognized the royal authority of Valikhan. In early January, it was established by the Qin emperor as Wali Khan. On February 23 of this year, he was confirmed as a khan of the Middle Zhuz by a special tsar's letter.

After his death, the sons of his second wife inherited. Genghis Valikhan, born to Gubaidullah and his younger wife Aiganym, was elected the first senior sultan of Kokshetau and Kushmurun districts.

The great Kazakh scientist Chokan Chingizovich Valikhanov is the grandson of Uali khan. The mausoleum is located in the village of Kazakhstan, Zerendi district.

Reference: Kazakhstan sacred objects
of whole national importance. – Astana: Foliant, 2017. –30-p.

zhanalyq-kentindegi-saiasi-qugyn-surgin-.name: Burial Place of Victims of Political Repression in Zhanalyk Populated Place
zhanalyq-kentindegi-saiasi-qugyn-surgin-.fact: The memorial complex, located in the village of Zhanalyk, Talgar district of Almaty region, is a place for victims of…
zhanalyq-kentindegi-saiasi-qugyn-surgin-.lead: The memorial complex, located in the village of Zhanalyk, Talgar district of Almaty region, is a place for victims of famine, innocent victims of political repressions in the 1930s and 1950s. More than 4,000 people are buried here.
zhanalyq-kentindegi-saiasi-qugyn-surgin-.bodyHtml:
The memorial complex, located in the village of Zhanalyk, Talgar district of Almaty region, is a place for victims of famine, innocent victims of political repressions in the 1930s and 1950s. More than 4,000 people are buried here.

It is a place where famous Kazakh people Saken Seifullin, Ilyas Zhansugurov, Beimbet Mailin and other statesmen of the republic were arrested, investigated and sentenced to death. In 1937-38, the NKVD shot these Kazakh intellectuals in one night and threw them at the foundations of crumbling houses in the village of Zhanalyk, knocking down the walls over the corpses.

From 1937 to 1946, the “Book of Mourning” was published, which included lists of those who were shot on political charges and buried near the village of Zhanalyk, Almaty region. The book states that four thousand one hundred and twenty-five people were shot.

Reference: Kazakhstan sacred objects
of whole national importance. – Astana: Foliant, 2017. –450-452-pp.

qapal-batyr-kesenesi.name: The Mausoleum of Kapal Batyr
qapal-batyr-kesenesi.fact: Kapal Batyr was an outstanding commander during the reign of his brothers Tauekel and Esim khans, who lived in the…
qapal-batyr-kesenesi.lead: Kapal Batyr was an outstanding commander during the reign of his brothers Tauekel and Esim khans, who lived in the late 16th and early 17th centuries.
qapal-batyr-kesenesi.bodyHtml:
Kapal Batyr was an outstanding commander during the reign of his brothers Tauekel and Esim khans, who lived in the late 16th and early 17th centuries. The mausoleum was built on the slopes of Eshkiolmes mountain, 80 km from Taldykorgan-Kapal road, Eskeldy district, Almaty region, over the grave of Kapal batyr Zhanysuly (1513-1606). The mausoleum is rectangular with five domes and is made of white silicate brick. The domes are made of metal structures and covered with galvanized copper.

He was a famous hero in the liberation of the Kazakh cities along the Syrdarya from the enemy and in the struggle against the Dzungar invasion in the east of the Kazakh Khanate. Chokan Valikhanov's unanimous opinion that "Kapal station is named after Kapal Batyr" in his "Dzungarian Essays" led to the discovery of Kapal Batyr's grave.

Reference: Kazakhstan sacred objects
of whole national importance. – Astana: Foliant,2017. –303-304-pp.

nauryzbai-quttymbetuly-kesenesi.name: Mausoleum of Nauryzbay Batyr Kuttymbetuly
nauryzbai-quttymbetuly-kesenesi.fact: The mausoleum is located south of Targap village of Zhambyl district of Almaty region on the road to the main hero…
nauryzbai-quttymbetuly-kesenesi.lead: The mausoleum is located south of Targap village of Zhambyl district of Almaty region on the road to the main hero, Degeres in the Kozybasy mountain. Nauryzbai Kuttymbetovich (1706-1781) - one of the three flag-bearing heroes of Abylai Khan (Karakerei Kabanbai, Kanzhigaly Bogenbai, Shapirashty Nauryzbai).
nauryzbai-quttymbetuly-kesenesi.bodyHtml:
The mausoleum is located south of Targap village of Zhambyl district of Almaty region on the road to the main hero, Degeres in the Kozybasy mountain. Nauryzbai Kuttymbetovich (1706-1781) - one of the three flag-bearing heroes of Abylai Khan (Karakerei Kabanbai, Kanzhigaly Bogenbai, Shapirashty Nauryzbai). Nauryzbai took part in the famous battle of Anyrakai. Batyr's life was spent in the war against the Dzungars. Nauryzbai's heroism in 1729, killing Kalmyk heroes Shamalkhan and Kaskelen in a battle, spread to the Kazakh steppes.

Literary and historical facts and legends of the country suggest that Nauryzbai Batyr became popular and proud in 1727-1731. One of the moments of Nauryzbai Batyr's life is recorded in the diary of Karl Miller, the ambassador of the Russian Empire to Kaldan Seren, a Dzungar settler, in the autumn of 1742.

Reference: Kazakhstan sacred objects
of whole national importance. – Astana: Foliant, 2017. –321-323-pp.

balgasyn-qorymy.name: Balgasyn Cemetery
balgasyn-qorymy.fact: Balgasyn is an ancient burial ground preserved from the Middle Ages, a monument of architecture.
balgasyn-qorymy.lead: Balgasyn is an ancient burial ground preserved from the Middle Ages, a monument of architecture. Aktobe region is located 55 km north of the modern city of Shalkar.
balgasyn-qorymy.bodyHtml:
Balgasyn is an ancient burial ground preserved from the Middle Ages, a monument of architecture. Aktobe region is located 55 km north of the modern city of Shalkar. The cemetery was studied in the late XIX and early XX centuries by members of the Orenburg Scientific Archive Commission A. Matov, I. Khokhlov, Zh. Castagne, in 1979-1980 an expedition of the Ministry of Culture of Kazakhstan (headed by S. Azhigaliyev). The cemetery consists of the remains of the Balgasyn tower, the mausoleum of Onalbek Ata (about XVII-XVIII centuries) and many tombs built of raw brick and slate.

The tower has long been considered a monument of the Kipchak era. As a result of research by the expedition of the Ministry of Culture of Kazakhstan, it was determined that the Balgasyn tower was built in the late XV and early XVI centuries of the Kazakh-Uzbek-Nogai epoch. In the descriptions of the tower before the fall (1900), especially in the painting by A. Matov (1897), the mausoleum clearly shows the features of the school of architects in the time of Amir Temir. The hammer tower is made of high quality baked brick and the dome is covered with blue enamel. The architecture of the Hammer Tower shows a compositional connection with the Mauerannahr and Desht Kipchak memorials.Archaeological excavations at the Balgasyn Tower in 2005, uncovered ceramics, pottery fragments, beads, rosaries, arrowheads and a 5-tiyn Russian coin dated 1859, a brick -kiln was found 400-500 m away. According to local legends, Balgasyn was built by his father at the burial place of an unknown pious girl. According to the second legend, the tower grew out of the ground by itself in three days. According to the third legend, the mausoleum was built of five thousand Tatars mixed with clay and mother's milk, made of baked bricks and left in an unknown direction. Ancient sources prove that the Kazakhs considered the monument to Balgasyn as sacred. Women who could not conceive believed that if they spent the night at the mausoleum and had a good dream, they would have a baby.

Reference: 1. Regional sacred sites of Kazakhstan. – Astana: Foliant, 2017. –131 p .;

  1. Sacred Kazakhstan. Volume 2 – Astana, 2018. –39 p.

botagoz-batyr-kesenesi.name: Mausoleum of Botagoz Batyr
botagoz-batyr-kesenesi.fact: Botakoz batyr, daughter of Tama Eset Kokiuly, daughter-in-law of Azhibai bi, lived in (1719-1747).
botagoz-batyr-kesenesi.lead: Botakoz batyr, daughter of Tama Eset Kokiuly, daughter-in-law of Azhibai bi, lived in (1719-1747).
botagoz-batyr-kesenesi.bodyHtml:
Botakoz batyr, daughter of Tama Eset Kokiuly, daughter-in-law of Azhibai bi, lived in (1719-1747).

Botakoz, the daughter of Tama Eset batyr, she was raised by her sister Zhapalak in her youth and learned martial arts from her. Even after the owl was handed over to Tleuli Batyr, they did not break up with him. She took part in expeditions with Tleuli Batyr in Zhapalak and amazed many Kalmyks with her sniper skills. Only after the birth of a child she paid attention to the upbringing of the child and rarely go to war.

In 1742, Eset batyr and Tleuli batyr were summoned by Abulkhair khan and they left. When the Dzungars found out, they attacked at night to take away the village horse. The Dzungars killed the persecutors who tried to snatch the horses from them. At that moment, Botakoz, dressed as a man, wearing a light armor, took up arms and went against the invaders with 150 soldiers. He attacked the Kazakh villages on the way to the Dzungarian Kalmyks, took a herd of horses and headed for his homeland. Suddenly “Karabura! Karabura! ” The young hero, who shouted: This Kalmyk leader was a Thai named Kondy. When the Kazakh troops surrounded him and tried to kill him, a young batyr, who had come out of one of them playing with a purple horse, put the bull in his hand and put it on his neck. When the Kalmyks saw that their commander had fallen to the ground, they fled and most of them were shot. Botakoz, the only daughter of the young Kazakh hero Tama Eset Tarkhan, is beautiful. The Kalmyk settler is very proud and humiliated that he lost to a Kazakh girl and became a prisoner. Hearing of his sister's victory, Zhapalak made a sacrifice and celebrated the victory in Kipchak. Valuable historical documents confirming this feat of Botakoz Esetkyzy are stored in the Aktobe regional museum. The mausoleum is located in Kemer village of Oil district.

Reference: 1. Regional sacred sites of Kazakhstan. –Astana: Foliant, 2017. –120 p;

doszhan-ishan-meshiti.name: Doszhan Ishan Mosque
doszhan-ishan-meshiti.fact: Doszhan Ishan Mosque is located in Temir district of Aktobe region.
doszhan-ishan-meshiti.lead: Doszhan Ishan Mosque is located in Temir district of Aktobe region. Doszhan Ishan (1815-1890) was a propagator of Islam in the territory of Western Kazakhstan.
doszhan-ishan-meshiti.bodyHtml:
Doszhan Ishan Mosque is located in Temir district of Aktobe region. Doszhan Ishan (1815-1890) was a propagator of Islam in the territory of Western Kazakhstan. He organized pilgrimages among the Kazakhs, built a takiya house for Kazakhs in the Arab world, Mecca, compiled the "Kazakh Chronicle" and demanded a "separate mufti for the Kazakhs" from the colonial government in the 80s of the XIX century, etc. He is one of the most famous figures in history.

He built a modern mosque near Shubarkuduk for a Burmese carpenter. One hundred people could pray freely in the mosque. In general, there is an opinion that the design of the mosque was based on the Yunusov Mosque in Kazan. Some speculate that it had six domes, while others suggested that it had nine domes. We believe that the idea of ​​"six domes" is true. It turned out that two colored bricks were used. The people will help with the main construction work. The interior of the mosque was decorated with ornaments, and the light from the outside illuminated all the patterns. The verses and hadiths are written in red. According to the information received to date, there was a madrasah for 150 children and a guest house near the mosque. The domes were demolished during the Soviet era.

Doszhan Ishan first went on pilgrimage at the age of 16, then in 1870-1874, and the third time in the mid-1880s. His descendants built a beautiful mosque on his burial ground, which is now a sacred place of pilgrimage.

Reference: Kazakhstan sacred objects
of whole national importance.. –Astana: Foliant, 2017. –p.286-288.

duisenbi-ahun-meshiti.name: Duysenbi Akhun Mosque
duisenbi-ahun-meshiti.fact: Duysenbi Imashuli (1865-1920) was a literate man who was fluent in Arabic, a mullah, he was aware of Russian and…
duisenbi-ahun-meshiti.lead: Duysenbi Imashuli (1865-1920) was a literate man who was fluent in Arabic, a mullah, he was aware of Russian and backward reading, and he was a saint. Duysenbi studied at a special religious madrasah in 1885-1886, and returned to the country in 1904.
duisenbi-ahun-meshiti.bodyHtml:
Duysenbi Imashuli (1865-1920) was a literate man who was fluent in Arabic, a mullah, he was aware of Russian and backward reading, and he was a saint. Duysenbi studied at a special religious madrasah in 1885-1886, and returned to the country in 1904. In 1908-1909, the villagers supported Duysenbi in opening a mosque. In 1913, the construction of the mosque was completed.Duysenbi was a prophet. When someone sick came to the mosque, he knew and felt it in advance. There is a legend that he caught two fairies and tied them to the door of the mosque. According to the elders, he used to walk around the mosque at night in a white shirt and white leggings. One day he said to his servant, “Let me take a look. You are guarding without sleeping. “If you fall asleep, I'm in danger”. When the servant fell asleep in the morning, the two fairies on the threshold flew away like swans. After this incident, Duysenbi was frustrated and he died in 1920. The mosque of Duysenbi akhun is an outstanding ritual monument of the North Aral Sea region. The mosque is located in Zhaysanbay aul of Irgiz district of Aktobe region.

Reference: 1. Regional sacred sites of Kazakhstan. –Astana: Foliant, 2017. –134 p.; 2. Sacred Kazakhstan. Volume 2 –Astana, 2018. –54 p.

zhanys-bi-kesenesi.name: Mausoleum of Zhanys Bi
zhanys-bi-kesenesi.fact: Zhanys bi Sygaiuly (1769-1867) is a famous bi, one of the most regarded people.
zhanys-bi-kesenesi.lead: Zhanys bi Sygaiuly (1769-1867) is a famous bi, one of the most regarded people. In the Irgiz region, the country became involved in governance early and came to power. He was an adjudication of great disputes between countries and tribes.
zhanys-bi-kesenesi.bodyHtml:
Zhanys bi Sygaiuly (1769-1867) is a famous bi, one of the most regarded people. In the Irgiz region, the country became involved in governance early and came to power. He was an adjudication of great disputes between countries and tribes. At the same time, Zhanys had a seal of the Kulaman tribe that was not approved by the Russian tsarist government of Altai branch. The seal was preserved until the 50-60s of the XX century.

The mausoleum of Zhanys Bi has become a sacred place. This mausoleum is a place of worship. The locals called it “Kyzyl Tam”. Those who go on a long journey, while waiting for blessings, come to the tomb of the saint, the grandfather of the bi, bow to the spirits, and the sick spend the night. The sincerity and justice of the Zhanys bi is described in parables: “Zhanys bi is not prejudice, the one that claims so does not have a faith”. The mausoleum is located 2 km from Zhanakurylys aul of Irgiz district of Aktobe region.

Reference: 1. Regional sacred sites of Kazakhstan. –Astana: Foliant, 2017. – 135 p.; 2. Sacred Kazakhstan. Volume 2 –Astana, 2018. –62 p.

isatai-haziret-meshiti.name: Isatai Hazrat Mosque
isatai-haziret-meshiti.fact: Isatai Hazrat Mosque is a monument located 7 km south-east of Zhaysanbay aul, Irgiz district, Aktobe region.According…
isatai-haziret-meshiti.lead: Isatai Hazrat Mosque is a monument located 7 km south-east of Zhaysanbay aul, Irgiz district, Aktobe region.According to folklore, the mosque was built by Agymbay, the son of a rich man named Shombal, for his father in the early ХХ century.
isatai-haziret-meshiti.bodyHtml:
Isatai Hazrat Mosque is a monument located 7 km south-east of Zhaysanbay aul, Irgiz district, Aktobe region.According to folklore, the mosque was built by Agymbay, the son of a rich man named Shombal, for his father in the early ХХ century. The mosque was built in the 1920s by a carpenter, his students Bisengali and Hasen. The bricks were fired from there. The mosque consisted of two rooms: the entrance and a large room. There were bookshelves in the entrance room. The walls are made of a mixture of raw bricks and baked red bricks. The tower is built next to the rooms. At the top of the conical tower, a circular staircase made of bricks leads to the place of call to prayer.Upon completion of the construction of the mosque, Saudabek Satbayuli, the elder of Irgiz uyezd, invited Isatai Satypaldiuli from Temir uyezd (about 1860-1930) and appointed him as an imam of the mosque. Since then, it has become known as the Isatai Mosque.

Reference: 1. Regional sacred sites of Kazakhstan. –Astana: Foliant, 2017. – 136 p.; 2. Sacred Kazakhstan. Volume 2 –Astana, 2018. –67 p.

keruen-sarai-tarihi-arhitekturalyq-keshe.name: Historical and Architectural Complex of Keruen Palace
keruen-sarai-tarihi-arhitekturalyq-keshe.fact: The caravanserai (mosque, shops, house of the fair committee, further complex) is located in the center of Oil…
keruen-sarai-tarihi-arhitekturalyq-keshe.lead: The caravanserai (mosque, shops, house of the fair committee, further complex) is located in the center of Oil district of Aktobe region.
keruen-sarai-tarihi-arhitekturalyq-keshe.bodyHtml:
The caravanserai (mosque, shops, house of the fair committee, further complex) is located in the center of Oil district of Aktobe region.

The first name of the complex was “Kokzhar fair”. The Kokzhar fair is a historical monument, which provided ample opportunities for the promotion of folk art and culture in Western Kazakhstan, it has saved elements of 13 fairs from all over Kazakhstan, the architecture of which has been preserved and not been destroyed.

Regulations on the Kokzhar fair were approved by the Russian Ministry of Internal Affairs on September 7, 1866 and were officially opened in the spring of 1867 in Kazbek bi volost of Temir district, Ural region. In 1867, the fair was attended by 137 traders. Goods worth about 250 thousand rubles were brought, of which more than 100 thousand rubles were sold and exchanged. Up to 20,000 different animals were purchased at the fair. Kokzhar fair is held twice a year (May 15 - June 15 and September 15 - October 15). In 1893, the Oyyl Mosque was built near the fair. Russian and Tatar traders from Orenburg, Sarytau and Samara came to the fair from the north, and caravans came from the south to establish contacts with Khiva, Bukhara, Turkmenistan and Afghanistan and Iran.

Livestock and livestock products were exported from Kokzhar to Taysoygan - Makat - Guryev, Astrakhan - North Caucasus, Azerbaijan, Iran. In 1867, 60 Tatars, 33 Russians and 22 Ural Cossacks took part in the fair. According to the Russian Statistics Committee in 1911, the turnover of the Kokzhar fair reached 2 million 140 thousand rubles.

Reference: 1. Regional sacred sites of Kazakhstan. –Astana: Foliant, 2017. –125 p.; 2. The sacred Kazakhstan. Volume 2 –Astana, 2018. – 69 p.

oiyl-meshiti.name: The Oiyl Mosque
oiyl-meshiti.fact: The Oiyl Mosque, one of the oldest and unique temples in Aktobe region.It was built in 1893.
oiyl-meshiti.lead: The Oiyl Mosque, one of the oldest and unique temples in Aktobe region.It was built in 1893. The mosque is located in the village of Oiyl, Oiyl district, Aktobe region.
oiyl-meshiti.bodyHtml:
The Oiyl Mosque, one of the oldest and unique temples in Aktobe region.It was built in 1893. The mosque is located in the village of Oiyl, Oiyl district, Aktobe region.

The foundation is made of natural stone, the belts are transported by camel cart from Orenburg, the base is made of red brick. The first chief imam Sagidulla Iztleuov was a literate man who spoke Arabic, Persian and Russian. In the 30s of the XX century, the religious symbols of the mosque were destroyed and it was turned into a drama theater, technical and economic warehouse. ⠀In the frame of independence, it was repaired in 1999 and rebuilt. It was overhauled in 2014.

One of the most popular legends about the history of the mosque is that the underground passage in Oiyl is connected with the mosque. Through this subway, merchants used to go to the markets and to the house of a rich merchant.

The first original dome of the mosque was made of silver, like a Muslim dome, and it used to have a large cross. Due to the legend during the years of political repression, the dome of the mosque was demolished and hidden in a local ravine.

Reference: Regional sacred sites of Kazakhstan. – Astana: Foliant, 2017. –126 p.

tamanyn-kok-meshiti.name: The Blue Mosque
tamanyn-kok-meshiti.fact: The Blue Mosque (early twentieth century) is a complex of mosques, madrassas and houses.
tamanyn-kok-meshiti.lead: The Blue Mosque (early twentieth century) is a complex of mosques, madrassas and houses. It is located in Or village of Mugalzhar district of Aktobe region. According to locals, the complex was built in 1902-1905 with funds raised from the Tama tribe, which is why the mosque is called the “Blue Mosque of Tama”. Initially, it was planned to build a mosque elsewhere, however the place was chosen since the voice was heard properly here.
tamanyn-kok-meshiti.bodyHtml:
The Blue Mosque (early twentieth century) is a complex of mosques, madrassas and houses. It is located in Or village of Mugalzhar district of Aktobe region. According to locals, the complex was built in 1902-1905 with funds raised from the Tama tribe, which is why the mosque is called the “Blue Mosque of Tama”. Initially, it was planned to build a mosque elsewhere, however the place was chosen since the voice was heard properly here.

This lone mosque on the Elek, Or, and Zhem rivers is a rectangular, one-story building that stretches from north to south. The foundation of the building is made of stone, the walls are made of treated black stone and clay. The roof of the building is covered with wooden beams, and the roof is covered with flat sheet metal. The general madrasah consists of four doors and seven window openings (one window on the east side turned into a door). At the opening ceremony of the mosque, Elder Tama Kosuak blessed for about an hour and a half. Tobazhan, who received his religious education from Bukhara, was the first imam of the mosque. People called him Sary Ishan. Tobazhan Ishan's voice was so loud that when he called for the morning prayer, his voice could be heard 15-20 km away.

All the residents of Emba and Ashysai villages went to the Blue Mosque for Friday prayers. During the Soviet era, Belyakov and Boranbay, the mosque's rulers, tore down the mosque's dome and dome with a tractor. But less than a year later, they both died with their entire family.

Currently, the walls of the mosque, which have been the heritage of our ancestors for centuries, are preserved intact. Near the mosque there is a stone madrasah where children once studied.

Reference: Regional sacred sites of Kazakhstan. –Astana: Foliant, 2017. –123 p; 2. The sacred Kazakhstan. Volume 2 – Astana: 2018. –109 p.

sundet-kesenesi.name: The Mausoleum of Sundet
sundet-kesenesi.fact: Sundet mausoleum (second half of the XIX century) is one of the octagonal, helmet-shaped architectural monuments.
sundet-kesenesi.lead: Sundet mausoleum (second half of the XIX century) is one of the octagonal, helmet-shaped architectural monuments. It is located 68 km south-west of Zharkamys village of Baiganin district of Aktobe region.
sundet-kesenesi.bodyHtml:
Sundet mausoleum (second half of the XIX century) is one of the octagonal, helmet-shaped architectural monuments. It is located 68 km south-west of Zharkamys village of Baiganin district of Aktobe region.

The mausoleum is located in Zharkamys village of Baiganin district. It is one of the outstanding monuments of ancient Kazakh architecture of Western Kazakhstan. The octagonal walls of the mausoleum resemble a yurt with a domed roof.

Sundet is a well-known figure in the Zhem-Sagyz region. According to folklore, the circumcision took place in the XIX century. He was a wealthy and respected cleric person. Sundet is remembered by the people as a just court and a mediator who settled various disputes among the people.

The mausoleum of Sundet was built in the XX century on the bank of the river Zhem by his son Agysbai and 5 grandsons after their return. According to assumptions of researchers M. Mendikulov and S.E. Azhigali, the monument is dated back to the second half of the XIX century. It is believed that the mausoleum was masterfully built by the national architect Dauletniyaz. The building, according to the master's plan, was built in an octagonal shape, unlike any other building in the region in terms of architectural features. There is no such mausoleum on the plateau of Zhem-Sagyz.

Reference: Regional sacred objects
of Kazakhstan. – Astana: Foliant, 2017. – 107 p.

toleubulaq-petroglifteri.name: Toleubulak Petroglyphs
toleubulaq-petroglifteri.fact: This complex is one of the archeological monuments of the ancient Stone Age of Kazakhstan.
toleubulaq-petroglifteri.lead: This complex is one of the archeological monuments of the ancient Stone Age of Kazakhstan. Toleubulak petroglyphs are located in Mugalzhar district of Aktobe region, 13 km north-east of Bulakty village, near Toleubulak wintering ground.
toleubulaq-petroglifteri.bodyHtml:
This complex is one of the archeological monuments of the ancient Stone Age of Kazakhstan. Toleubulak petroglyphs are located in Mugalzhar district of Aktobe region, 13 km north-east of Bulakty village, near Toleubulak wintering ground. The petroglyphs of the cave were discovered in 2000 by a joint international Kazakh-Russian expedition to study the Stone Age settlements in Mugalzhar district (leaders: Academician of the Russian Academy of Sciences, archeologist A.P. Derevyanko, Professor V.T. Petrin, Zh.K. Taimagambetov, etc.). , introduced into science. In 2006, a specialist of the Institute of Archeology named after A. Margulan, Candidate of Historical Sciences Z. Samashev conducted research.The monument is an ancient painting (petroglyphs) in the cave Toleubulak near the Mugalzhar Mountains in the upper reaches of the river Zhem. The Toleubulak monument was considered a sacred place in the life of the first society and may have served as a coffin (for the cave to perform rituals related to fertility and water properties). This is evidenced by the pictures at the bottom of the cave, which are 6 cm deep and 17-25 cm in diameter. In a small cave there are petroglyphs, anthropomorphs and deep lines resembling hooves and mushrooms. Scientists believe that the above symbols may be common in the Paleolithic, Mesolithic and Neolithic.Toleubulak cave and its surroundings have been of interest to people since ancient times. Near the monument, there are workshops with Paleolithic sites and stone artifacts.

Reference: 1. Regional sacred sites of Kazakhstan. –Astana: Foliant, 2017. –124 p .; 2. The sacred Kazakhstan. Volume 2 –Astana, 2018. –117 p.

han-molasy-qorymy-memorialdyq-kesheni.name: Memorial Complex “Khan Molasy” (Abulkair Khan, XVIII century)
han-molasy-qorymy-memorialdyq-kesheni.fact: Khan's tomb is a Kazakh cemetery that appeared in the XVIII century.
han-molasy-qorymy-memorialdyq-kesheni.lead: Khan's tomb is a Kazakh cemetery that appeared in the XVIII century. It is located 4 km from the confluence of the river Kabyrga and Ulkeyek in Aiteke bi district of Aktobe region.
han-molasy-qorymy-memorialdyq-kesheni.bodyHtml:
Khan's tomb is a Kazakh cemetery that appeared in the XVIII century. It is located 4 km from the confluence of the river Kabyrga and Ulkeyek in Aiteke bi district of Aktobe region.

“Khan's tomb” occupies 16.0 hectares, including thousands of graves. According to A. Levshin and N. Rychkov, the khan of the Junior zhuz Abulkhair was buried in this cemetery.

Abulkhair Muhammad Kazy Bahadur Khan (1693-1748) - khan of the Junior zhuz, who ruled in 1718-1748. Commander-in-Chief of the Kazakh troops. Abulkhair Khan is considered to be the pride of our nation for his contribution as a prominent statesman, public service in international relations, political initiatives, the way of governing the state during the establishment of the khanate. The memorial complex is a symbol of national identity and unity, it is worshiped as a symbolic object.

Reference: Kazakhstan sacred objects
of whole national importance. – Astana: Foliant, 2017. – 338-340 pp.

qulshan-ata-zherasty-meshiti.name: Kulshan Ata Underground Mosque
qulshan-ata-zherasty-meshiti.fact: It is located 67 km east of Kulsary, Zhylyoi district, Atyrau region.
qulshan-ata-zherasty-meshiti.lead: It is located 67 km east of Kulsary, Zhylyoi district, Atyrau region. The underground mosque was built by Kulshan Ata (XVIII-XIX centuries), known for his niece and disciple Beket Myrzaguly.
qulshan-ata-zherasty-meshiti.bodyHtml:
It is located 67 km east of Kulsary, Zhylyoi district, Atyrau region. The underground mosque was built by Kulshan Ata (XVIII-XIX centuries), known for his niece and disciple Beket Myrzaguly.A. Alekseev, a Russian topographer who visited the mosque in the 1950s, wrote about the first construction of the mosque: "... the mosque, built with a chalky roof, consists of two parts, which are 7 inches apart." In the first part, religious rites were performed, and in the second part, the body of the deceased was wrapped in a shroud. Legend has it that the owner of the mosque, a saint named Kulshan, lived in a room of the mosque when he was old enough, and was later buried there. His body was found in the underground mosque in 1851-1852 by the above-mentioned Russian topographer.In recent years, a two-room mosque has been built to preserve the mosque. The first is the entrance room, the second is domed with shells, through which you can enter the first two rooms of the underground mosque. The head of a separate four-sided stone in front of the mosque is cut out in a triangle and the inscription "Kulshan Ata" is written on it. A dark house has been built nearby for a long time, it has a lighthouse and the house is well equipped.Saint Kulshan lived around the end of the ХVІІІ century and the beginning of the ХІХ century. According to one source, the saint graduated from religious schools in Bukhara and Khiva. There are three different accounts of his relationship to Beket Ata: Alekseev's writings state that Kulshan was a disciple of Beket Ata, another version says that Aulie Ata was one of Beket Ata's 92 disciples, "Beket's son-in-law", and the third describes him as "Beket's nephew". There is a saying of Beket: "Anyone who comes to me from the west will first spend the night with the saint Kulshan". There was a snake in the saint's bed, and on Thursdays and Fridays there were fires.Kulshan also taught children like Beket, who went down in history as one of the first Arabic literate people in the Kazakh steppes.

Reference: Kazakhstan sacred objects
of whole national importance. – Astana: Foliant, 2017. – 258-259-pp.

murat-monkeuly-kesenesi.name: Mausoleum of Murat Monkeuly
murat-monkeuly-kesenesi.fact: The burial place of the poet Murat Monkeuly is located 3 km northeast of Zharsuat aul of Inder district of Atyrau…
murat-monkeuly-kesenesi.lead: The burial place of the poet Murat Monkeuly is located 3 km northeast of Zharsuat aul of Inder district of Atyrau region.Murat Monkeuly (1843-1906) - aitysker akyn, zhyrau.
murat-monkeuly-kesenesi.bodyHtml:
The burial place of the poet Murat Monkeuly is located 3 km northeast of Zharsuat aul of Inder district of Atyrau region.Murat Monkeuly (1843-1906) - aitysker akyn, zhyrau. One of the most famous figures in the history of Kazakh literature, one of the most famous poets of "Zar Zaman". In his youth, Eset followed the example of the famous orator, the heroes grew up memorizing songs. The most valuable works of Kazakh poetry are "Ush kiyan", "Death", "Saryarka", "Kyz", "What do you need to give a horse?", "Will the horse be beautiful?", "False science is false", etc. author of voluminous works.The name of Murat Monkeuly remained in the history of literature not only as a great master of the art of aitys, but also as a great epic poet. Monkeuly, who was known for his courage, quick-wittedness and ingenuity, was always seen from the heights.Murat Monkeuly longed for the independence of his country and sang songs against expansion. Complaining about the colonial plunder of the settlement, the poet remembered the past of the steppe where he was born and grew up. According to him, “First, the Russians conquered the Volga, took the lands of Sarytau and Ashtarkhan. All the water and water were captured by the Russians, and the Kazakhs were swallowed up by it "," Kazakh land and heritage "," Where does a large settlement find? " The lines of the poem testify to the poet's patriotic spirit.The works of Sypyra Zhyrau, Asan Kaigy, Kaztugan, Zhiembet, Shalkiiz and other historical figures have reached us with the words of the poet Murat. His contribution to the delivery of Makhambet's poems is especially significant.

Reference: 1. Kazakhstan sacred objects
of whole national importance. – Astana: Foliant, 2017. –153-p.; 2.The sacred Kazakhstan Volume -2. –Astana, 2018. –207-p.

onai-ata-kesenesi.name: Onai Ata Mausoleum
onai-ata-kesenesi.fact: The mausoleum is located on the Atyrau-Makat highway in Atyrau region, 60 km from the aul of Makat.According to…
onai-ata-kesenesi.lead: The mausoleum is located on the Atyrau-Makat highway in Atyrau region, 60 km from the aul of Makat.According to sources, Onai Esimbetuli (1823-1900) was a kind, benevolent and intelligent man.
onai-ata-kesenesi.bodyHtml:
The mausoleum is located on the Atyrau-Makat highway in Atyrau region, 60 km from the aul of Makat.According to sources, Onai Esimbetuli (1823-1900) was a kind, benevolent and intelligent man. It is said that in his time he was a counselor of the Issyk tribe, a man of authority who could listen to those around him. The generous man who took care of the passengers along the way was a wealthy man who lived on the seashore in the winter and in the summer, summer and autumn along the rivers Oil, Kiel and Sagyz. He was respected by the people for his kindness and compassion for the poor.There is a dark house and a mosque at the burial place of Onai Ata. The mausoleum of Onai Ata is a place where passengers pass by. Legend has it that he was so powerful that if he did not recognize the ghost, he would overturn the car.

Reference: 1. Kazakhstan sacred objects
of whole national importance. – Astana: Foliant, 2017. –163-p.; 2.The sacred Kazakhstan Volume -2. –Astana, 2018. –213-p.

baibaraq-batyr-qudaiqululy-kesenesi.name: Battle of Batyrbaybarak Kudaikululy
baibaraq-batyr-qudaiqululy-kesenesi.fact: The mausoleum is located in Baibarak cemetery, 16 km from Bazarsholpan village of Akzhayik district of West Kazakhstan…
baibaraq-batyr-qudaiqululy-kesenesi.lead: The mausoleum is located in Baibarak cemetery, 16 km from Bazarsholpan village of Akzhayik district of West Kazakhstan region. It looks like a hero's helmet, the size of an eight-winged yurt.
baibaraq-batyr-qudaiqululy-kesenesi.bodyHtml:
The mausoleum is located in Baibarak cemetery, 16 km from Bazarsholpan village of Akzhayik district of West Kazakhstan region. It looks like a hero's helmet, the size of an eight-winged yurt. The exterior is decorated like elements of a yurt. The facade depicts a man's weapon - five weapons. It is built of white stone of the plateau.Baibarak Kudaikululi (lived about the beginning of the XVIII century) - a hero, a person whose name became the motto of the country. Historian Isatai Kenzhaliyev was the first to write the history of the Baibarak motto on the basis of genealogical data preserved in the memory of the country. According to him, 14-year-old Baibarak, who was captured during the Kalmyk invasion of the Kazakh steppes, was released with his courage, bravery and courage. "How would you thank me if I sent you home?" "I would shout" Baibarak "and kill your country!" that is. After arriving in the country, he managed to fight the Kalmyks, received a blessing from Seitimbet Batyr, and soon arrested the Kalmyk leader. This is Baibarak's first feat. When he delivered the victory message to Seitimbet, he said, “I am getting old. Now the motto of the Alasha people is "Baibarak".Thus, the word "Baibarak" became the motto of Alasha, and in many difficult times became the foundation of the village, the catalyst for the preservation of the unity of the country. In many battles and gatherings there are moments when the motto of all Alshyn, Baiuly, Sultansiyk with five grandfathers. There are no bones of the hero under the mausoleum. The hero was buried near the cemetery where Baibarak was buried.

References: 1. Kazakhstan sacred objects
of whole national importance. – Astana: Foliant, 2017. – 181-p.; 2.The sacred Kazakhstan. Volume-2. –Astana: 2018. –252-p.

bokei-ordasy-tarihi-kesheni.name: Historical Complex “Bokei Ordasi”
bokei-ordasy-tarihi-kesheni.fact: The historical-museum complex “Bokei Ordasy” is located in the village of Khan Ordasy, Bokei Ordasy district, 550 km…
bokei-ordasy-tarihi-kesheni.lead: The historical-museum complex “Bokei Ordasy” is located in the village of Khan Ordasy, Bokei Ordasy district, 550 km from the center of the West Kazakhstan region.
bokei-ordasy-tarihi-kesheni.bodyHtml:
The historical-museum complex “Bokei Ordasy” is located in the village of Khan Ordasy, Bokei Ordasy district, 550 km from the center of the West Kazakhstan region. The Inner Kazakh or Bokei Horde is a historical place founded by Bokei and renewed by Zhangir. On the territory of the historical-museum complex there are monuments of the XIX century, preserved to this day and under state protection. The historical buildings, which are historical and architectural monuments, are combined.

Built in 1828, Khan Zhangir Palace is the only khan's palace preserved in Kazakhstan. The first fair in Kazakhstan, a school, a pharmacy, a hospital, a treasury, a girls' school, a fire station, a printing house, an anti-plague station and other institutions were built under the sky museum. like finished artifacts inside. Khan's buildings, a shopping mall, a hospital complex, and a school campus are still preserved in the Khan's rate, which was founded by Zhangir Khan, or in the Khan's Horde as it is now called. The historical and museum complex of Bokei Horde includes the Khan's Palace, the house of the doctor A.A. Sergachev, built in the XIX century, the mosque rebuilt on the project of the Khan Mosque, built in 1835, the building of the Treasury, opened in 1867, Targyn School in 1868, opened in 1883. There is a school building, five houses of the school campus of the XIX century, two hospital buildings opened in 1852 and a pantheon of mausoleums of Khan Zhangir, kuishi D. Shigayev, scientist M.S. Babazhanov, located 4 km from the village.

The historical-museum complex of Bokei Horde begins with the Horde Historical and Revolutionary Museum, which was opened in 1962 on a public basis on the occasion of the 45th anniversary of the October Revolution. Due to the increase in the number of buildings belonging to the museum, the Museum of the History of the Horde was raised in 2002 to the status of a historical and museum complex of the Bokei Horde. In the building of the Treasury in the historical-museum complex of Bokei Horde there are museums “History of Bokei Horde”, which tell about the 200-year history of Bokei Horde, in the Khan Mosque - "Independence", in the eastern wing of the Khan's Palace – “Chamber of Arms in the Khan's Palace”. The Museum of Public Education in Bokei Horde was opened in 2007 at the Girls' School, which was reconstructed on the basis of the state program “Cultural Heritage”. The political and ideological activity of the later Alash intellectuals was closely connected with this horde.

In 2003, the Bokei Horde Historical and Museum Complex was accepted as a member of the International Council of Museums (ICOM) and registered in Paris.

References: 1. Kazakhstan sacred objects
of whole national importance. – Astana: Foliant, 2017. – 443-445-pp.
