araltobe-kesheni.name: Araltobe Complex
araltobe-kesheni.fact: It is located 70 km east of Kulsary, Zhylyoi district of Atyrau region. Chronological period B.C. IV-B.C. II century.
araltobe-kesheni.lead: It is located 70 km east of Kulsary, Zhylyoi district of Atyrau region. Chronological period B.C. IV-B.C. II century. The group of Araltobe burial mounds was discovered in 1989 by the West Kazakhstan archeological expedition.
araltobe-kesheni.bodyHtml:
It is located 70 km east of Kulsary, Zhylyoi district of Atyrau region. Chronological period B.C. IV-B.C. II century. The group of Araltobe burial mounds was discovered in 1989 by the West Kazakhstan archeological expedition. In 1989, the West Kazakhstan archeological expedition led by Z. Samashev excavated the Araltobe burial mounds. The necropolis is divided into four parts, which probably represent the four seasons of the year. In addition, the sun is divided into 12 parts. This year may mean “12 months”. The top of the mound is covered with flat stones in a shell-like manner.In the first of the three excavations, human skeletons and fragments of glass beads and arrowheads were found. From the second mound there was a corpse with its head facing south, next to it there was a box with more than a hundred arrows, a large side pottery jar and an iron sword. Before that, the Alans lived in the period of the sword, etc. The sword, found in the Zhylyoi region in the IV-V centuries, allows us to trace the origin of this weapon to four or five centuries and connect it with the history of the Sarmatians who inhabited this region.The second man in gold in the history of Kazakhstan was found in the third excavated necropolis. In addition to the corpses of men and women, two horses and an eagle were buried at their feet. Men's clothing is adorned with gold ornaments, and even a bundle of hair, weapons, fringes, and the image of a samruk on a cane are covered with gold. This may prove that the man was a tribal leader, a commander, or a clergyman.

Reference: Kazakhstan sacred objects
of whole national importance. – Astana: Foliant, 2017. – 88-89 pp.

zhympitydagy-alashorda-uii.name: Alashorda House in Zhympity
zhympitydagy-alashorda-uii.fact: In the village of Zhympity (Syrym district of West Kazakhstan region), the western wing of the Alashorda government…
zhympitydagy-alashorda-uii.lead: In the village of Zhympity (Syrym district of West Kazakhstan region), the western wing of the Alashorda government, the center of the western Alashorda, there are several buildings related to the history of Alash.The government of the Western Alash Horde, headed by Zhahansha and Khalel Dosmukhamedov in 1918-1919, is located in this historic building.
zhympitydagy-alashorda-uii.bodyHtml:
In the village of Zhympity (Syrym district of West Kazakhstan region), the western wing of the Alashorda government, the center of the western Alashorda, there are several buildings related to the history of Alash.The government of the Western Alash Horde, headed by Zhahansha and Khalel Dosmukhamedov in 1918-1919, is located in this historic building. In 1917-1918, when the people of Alash achieved independence, the western wing of Alashorda had the longest life: 19 months - 578 days.The building was built in 1867, a two-storey wooden house, the walls are made of straw and the outer floor is covered with boards. After the construction of this building, a Russian merchant built a mechanical grain mill in the late 1890s. There he harvested the most expensive quality grain from soybeans and sold it to Orenburg and Uralsk. In July 1917, the Alash Party was formed. From February 1918 to October 1920 the government of “Alashorda” was located in this building.Today in this building there is a hall "Alash" of the Museum of History and Local Lore named after Syrym Datuly, which was opened in honor of the 95th anniversary of Alashorda.

Reference: Kazakhstan sacred objects
of whole national importance. – Astana: Foliant, 2017. –458-460-pp.

taqsai-kesheni.name: Taksai Complex
taqsai-kesheni.fact: The complex is located on the territory of Dolinny rural district of Terekty district of West Kazakhstan region.
taqsai-kesheni.lead: The complex is located on the territory of Dolinny rural district of Terekty district of West Kazakhstan region. Chronological date: VI -V BC centuries.During archeological excavations in 2012, the West Kazakhstan regional center of history and archeology discovered five Taksai burial mounds.
taqsai-kesheni.bodyHtml:
The complex is located on the territory of Dolinny rural district of Terekty district of West Kazakhstan region.

Chronological date: VI -V BC centuries.During archeological excavations in 2012, the West Kazakhstan regional center of history and archeology discovered five Taksai burial mounds. The burial place of an aristocratic woman was opened in the № 6 settlement of the Taksai-I mound complex. Golden jewelry of a woman, stickers on her clothes, remnants of a special pig-roofed hat, a comb with the image of a war scene, ritual items and household items were found in the grave.Specialists headed by Kazakh scientist-restorer Krym Altynbek worked on the restoration of the "Golden Princess" found in the Taksai mound. The construction of materials and burial elements, ritual items, the burial of two guards showed that the woman had a special status and a high status in society. Among them is a rare and amazing comb - "Taksai comb". This is a very rare artifact in terms of the date of its creation and the appearance of ancient people. In the comb it must have depicted one of the greatest historical events of the first millennium BC, the conflict between the two worlds between the Achaemenids and the steppe nomads of Iran.

zhaiyq-qalashygy.name: Zhayk Town
zhaiyq-qalashygy.fact: The center of the West Kazakhstan region is located 12 km southeast of the city of Uralsk.
zhaiyq-qalashygy.lead: The center of the West Kazakhstan region is located 12 km southeast of the city of Uralsk. Chronological period: XIII-XIV centuries.During the Golden Horde, the Urals was a civilized city with its own production and handicrafts.
zhaiyq-qalashygy.bodyHtml:
The center of the West Kazakhstan region is located 12 km southeast of the city of Uralsk. Chronological period: XIII-XIV centuries.During the Golden Horde, the Urals was a civilized city with its own production and handicrafts. Among the public buildings found in the Ural town, the bath-bath aroused interest. The bath is located at a depth of 150-170 cm above ground level. The total area of the bath is 110-170 square meters.Archaeological excavations have proved that the Ural settlement is a remnant of the developed Golden Horde. One of the two copper coins found has the inscription "737 minted in the palace" (1336-1337 ). This money was used by the Golden Horde in 1312-1357. It was issued during the reign of the Uzbek khan. As in the case of the Urals, the bathhouse is still preserved in the East, and the brick kiln was probably brought to the cities of the Golden Horde on the Volga and the Urals from Central Asia and South Kazakhstan. During the Golden Horde, such furnaces were known in Khorezm, in the ancient settlements of Otrar and Kuyriktobe.

gumar-qarashtyn-zherlengen-zheri.name: The Burial Place of Gumar Karash
gumar-qarashtyn-zherlengen-zheri.fact: The burial place of Gumar Karash is in the territory of Talov rural district of Zhanibek district of West Kazakhstan…
gumar-qarashtyn-zherlengen-zheri.lead: The burial place of Gumar Karash is in the territory of Talov rural district of Zhanibek district of West Kazakhstan region.Gumar Karash (1875-1921) - an outstanding poet of the Kazakh people, folklorist, religious and public figure, Alashorda member, educator.
gumar-qarashtyn-zherlengen-zheri.bodyHtml:
The burial place of Gumar Karash is in the territory of Talov rural district of Zhanibek district of West Kazakhstan region.Gumar Karash (1875-1921) - an outstanding poet of the Kazakh people, folklorist, religious and public figure, Alashorda member, educator. He is a person who skillfully combines civic pride and delicate lyricism in his work, a philosopher, a man who has become a golden bridge between the Western mentality and the established religious principles of the East. He first studied at a local madrassa, then at a madrassa in Ufa, where he reportedly continued his education in Istanbul.Gumar Karash was the first Kazakh member of the Spiritual Council of Muslims of the Eastern part of the Russian Empire. Gumar Karash, a supporter of the Alash party and the government, was strongly opposed to the violent overthrow of the existing structure in society. In this regard, he published a collection of poems "Citizens of Alash", "What am I afraid of", "The sun was born". However, he soon became involved in the struggle against the Sovietization of the village. Gumar Karash is a representative of the Jadid movement, who opened the Tlenshisai Jadid school in Kaztalovka district. He advocated the introduction of modern advanced processes - economic and cultural-educational mechanisms, the development of national culture.

qarlag-dolinka-kenti.lead: The museum of remembrance for the victims of political repressions, located in the village of Dolinka, Karaganda region, is the most famous correctional labor camp in Kazakhstan.
qarlag-dolinka-kenti.bodyHtml:
The museum of remembrance for the victims of political repressions, located in the village of Dolinka, Karaganda region, is the most famous correctional labor camp in Kazakhstan. Many talented and intelligent sons of the Kazakh people are known as “counter-revolutionary assassins”, “organizers of terrorist acts”, “Japanese spies”, etc. was the victim of fabricated accusations. They tried to confess to their "crimes" using torture methods that were officially allowed. The whole country considered them “enemies of the people” and tried to deprive their children of their parents and their wives of their spouses. The years 1937-1938 were the culmination of the political violence perpetrated by Stalin's brutal regime, which massacred innocent people.On April 5, 1997, the Decree of the President of the Republic of Kazakhstan “On declaring May 31 the Day of Remembrance of Victims of Political Repressions” was issued.

tungysh-prezident-tarihi-madeni-ortalygy.name: Historical and Cultural Center of the First President
tungysh-prezident-tarihi-madeni-ortalygy.fact: The historical and cultural center of the First President was opened in Temirtau, Karaganda region in 2011 with the…
tungysh-prezident-tarihi-madeni-ortalygy.lead: The historical and cultural center of the First President was opened in Temirtau, Karaganda region in 2011 with the participation of the Head of State. The center is aimed at spiritual formation, spiritual, moral and patriotic education of Kazakhstanis, as well as access to national and world art and culture.
tungysh-prezident-tarihi-madeni-ortalygy.bodyHtml:
The historical and cultural center of the First President was opened in Temirtau, Karaganda region in 2011 with the participation of the Head of State. The center is aimed at spiritual formation, spiritual, moral and patriotic education of Kazakhstanis, as well as access to national and world art and culture.The center has six exhibition halls, which tell the story of the formation of independent Kazakhstan and the life and work of the President. The first hall is called “Independent Kazakhstan”. The exhibits in the hall tell the story of the first years of independence of the country.The second hall is called “Child of his time”. There are photos and documents related to the future President's youth, parents, place of birth, school days and education at the №8 technical school in Dneprodzerzhinsk, Ukraine.In the third hall “Personality”. There are exhibits related to the beginning of N. Nazarbayev's career at the Karaganda Metallurgical Plant, his student years, the formation of the family of the future President. The fourth hall is called “Kazakhstan's steel face”. Here is a complete set of metallurgical production using new innovative technologies. The fifth hall “In the course of time” There is valuable information about the beginning of N.Nazarbayev's political career, from the first secretary of the Komsomol Committee of Temirtau to his election as the First President of Kazakhstan.The sixth hall is called “Kazakhstan's way”. There are exhibits about the creative work carried out in the country under the leadership of the President since the independence of Kazakhstan, significant socio-political events and economic achievements in Kazakhstan during the years of independence.

qunanbai-qazhy-meshiti.name: Kunanbay Hajji Mosque
qunanbai-qazhy-meshiti.fact: Kunanbay Hajji Mosque, located in Karkaralinsk, Karaganda region, is a religious building carved from wood.
qunanbai-qazhy-meshiti.lead: Kunanbay Hajji Mosque, located in Karkaralinsk, Karaganda region, is a religious building carved from wood. Construction of the mosque began in 1851 and was completed in 1951.
qunanbai-qazhy-meshiti.bodyHtml:
Kunanbay Hajji Mosque, located in Karkaralinsk, Karaganda region, is a religious building carved from wood. Construction of the mosque began in 1851 and was completed in 1951. Later, a madrasah, a dormitory for students and a house for mullahs were built near the mosque.

Kunanbay Hajji Uskenbayuli (1804-1886), the father of the great poet Abai, was a bi, wrestler and senior sultan. One of the most memorable and legendary works in Kunanbay's biography is the construction of a mosque in Karkaralinsk and the construction of a house for Muslims who went on pilgrimage to Mecca.The mosque of Kunanbay Uskenbayev in Karkaralinsk is a two-storey wooden building. Unfortunately, the mosque of Kunanbay Uskenbayev did not remained in its original state. The mosque was demolished in 1920, the building was used by the Soviet authorities as a school, then transferred to warehouses, and even later became vacant. In the 1980s, the Kunanbay Mosque was completely restored.

zhoshy-han-kesenesi.name: Mausoleum of Jochi Khan
zhoshy-han-kesenesi.fact: Karaganda region is an ancient architectural monument located 50 km northeast of Zhezkazgan, on the banks of the river…
zhoshy-han-kesenesi.lead: Karaganda region is an ancient architectural monument located 50 km northeast of Zhezkazgan, on the banks of the river Kengir. The mausoleum was dedicated to Genghis Khan's son Jochi Khan, the founder of the Golden Horde.
zhoshy-han-kesenesi.bodyHtml:
Karaganda region is an ancient architectural monument located 50 km northeast of Zhezkazgan, on the banks of the river Kengir. The mausoleum was dedicated to Genghis Khan's son Jochi Khan, the founder of the Golden Horde.Jochi Khan (1187-1227) - the founder of a new state in the Kipchak steppes after the Mongol invasion - the founder of the Jochi ulus, the eldest of Genghis Khan's four sons Jochi ruled all the lands from the Irtysh to the Ural Mountains and further west.

The Horde is located along the Irtysh River (Altyn Orda).The study of the mazar begins with an article by Sh. Valikhanov “On the tombs of the Kyrgyz Kaisak and the former in general”. (1855). In 1868, in the work of Lieutenant Colonel Krasovsky “Area of the Siberian Kyrgyz” there is a description of ancient construction.

alasha-han-kesenesi.name: Alasha Khan Mausoleum
alasha-han-kesenesi.fact: It is located in the valley of the river Karakengir in Ulytau district of Karaganda region, 2 km from the right bank…
alasha-han-kesenesi.lead: It is located in the valley of the river Karakengir in Ulytau district of Karaganda region, 2 km from the right bank, near the aul Malshybay. The monument dates back to the XI-XII centuries.
alasha-han-kesenesi.bodyHtml:
It is located in the valley of the river Karakengir in Ulytau district of Karaganda region, 2 km from the right bank, near the aul Malshybay. The monument dates back to the XI-XII centuries. Built in honor of Alasha Khan. His name is directly connected with the appearance of three Kazakh zhuzs. In the ethnogenesis of the Kazakh people, before the Kazakhs were called Kazakhs, in the IX-X centuries its first name was "Alash". Alasha (Alash) khan is the ancestor of the tribes that, according to folklore, formed the "Six Alash".

Alasha khan is a great figure, a hero, a bi and a ruler of the nation, who united the nomadic Turks and created the first Alash (Kazakh) state.The place where Rashid ad-Din and Abelgazy Alasha khan lived is described as the central part of Desht Kipchak. According to Chokan Valikhanov, one of the khans of Turkestan (Kyzyl Arslan) gave birth to a child and named him "Alasha". In a short time, young men gathered around him, and his reputation in the country grew. Alasha was an educated and wise man, so he put him in the alasha and raised him as a khan. The word "Alty Alash" means six tribes that followed the six sons of Oguz. After the fall of the Golden Horde, "Alash" became a motto uniting nomadic Kazakhs. In the mythopoetic environment, he was at the forefront of a significant event for the whole nation and was the catalyst.

dombauyl-guryptyq-eskertkishi.name: Dombauyl Ceremonial Monument
dombauyl-guryptyq-eskertkishi.fact: The monument is located 58 km northwest of Zhezkazgan, Ulytau district of Karaganda region, on the right bank of the…
dombauyl-guryptyq-eskertkishi.lead: The monument is located 58 km northwest of Zhezkazgan, Ulytau district of Karaganda region, on the right bank of the river Karakengir. Chronological period: VIII-IX centuries.
dombauyl-guryptyq-eskertkishi.bodyHtml:
The monument is located 58 km northwest of Zhezkazgan, Ulytau district of Karaganda region, on the right bank of the river Karakengir. Chronological period: VIII-IX centuries. The Dombauyl monument was studied by the Central Kazakhstan archeological expedition led by Alkei Margulan in 1946-1947.

The mausoleum is built of stone slabs with a conical (pig-shaped) rectangular base with a height of more than 5 meters. Among the Kazakhs, stone mausoleums with domes resembling such yurts were called "uytas", "trunk". According to scholars, the Dombauyl mausoleum was built during the reign of the Huns. According to legend, this mausoleum was built in honor of the great composer and warrior Dombauyl, and its existence is associated with history and myth (fairy tale). According to the legends of the Kazakh people, Dombauyl is a hero from Naiman. It seems that Dombauyl was a reliable companion of Jochi khan, a palace sniper. This is because the tomb of Jochi Khan and the mausoleum of Dombauyl are very close. Dombauyldai glorified the name of the hero, his two sons - Ket-Buka and Kel-Buka - were daulesker kuishi. There are speculations that the author of the kui "Aksak Kulan" is Ket-Buka, the son of Dombauyl. When the famous historian Kurbangali Khalitovich described the formation of the "Eight Oguz", the name of the tribe with a negative connotation was Dombauyl.According to Serik Gabdullin, Dombauyl Batyr is said to be an influential man on the right knee of Genghis Khan. Genghis Khan, who appreciated Dombauyl and understood his qualities, joined him as a counselor to his eldest son Jochi. Dombauyl was Genghis Khan's sniper. Dombauyl was always with him when the khan built a hut and went hunting. Baiterek was a great sniper, a famous hero, a kuishi, a composer who played the dombra and kobyz.

terekti-aulie-petroglifteri.name: Petroglyphs of Saint Terekty
terekti-aulie-petroglifteri.fact: Saint Terekty is located 85 km from Zhezkazgan, Karaganda region, 20 km northwest of Terekty station.
terekti-aulie-petroglifteri.lead: Saint Terekty is located 85 km from Zhezkazgan, Karaganda region, 20 km northwest of Terekty station. Chronological period: Bronze Age (beginning of 2-1 millennium BCE);
terekti-aulie-petroglifteri.bodyHtml:
Saint Terekty is located 85 km from Zhezkazgan, Karaganda region, 20 km northwest of Terekty station.

Chronological period: Bronze Age (beginning of 2-1 millennium BCE); to the Scythian-Siberian epoch (XII BCE - I century BCE) and the Middle Ages.Along with the petroglyphs of antiquity, the "Saint Terekty" is a sacred place where traces of precious metals and various mounds were found in the Early Iron Age. The most common petroglyph is a picture of a horse. There are also pictures of camels, bulls, goats, deer, snakes, cats, as well as carts with two horses. And the abundance of various symbols and signs, geometric figures testify to the fact that this place was an altar in ancient times. Here you can see the divine, mythological, religious and philosophical worldviews of the nomads through the images of animals and the 12-year calendar. Traces of the Saint Terekty have become the basis for many myths and legends.

qorasan-ata-kesenesi.name: Korasan Ata Mausoleum
qorasan-ata-kesenesi.fact: Kyzylorda region is located about 15 km from the village of Zhanakorgan. Khorasan Ata lived in the IX century.
qorasan-ata-kesenesi.lead: Kyzylorda region is located about 15 km from the village of Zhanakorgan. Khorasan Ata lived in the IX century. Abd al-Jalil Bab Khorasan Ata is the fifth generation of Muhammad al-Hanafiya, the son of Ali ibn Abu Talib (Hazrat Ali), according to the genealogy of Nasab-nama.
qorasan-ata-kesenesi.bodyHtml:
Kyzylorda region is located about 15 km from the village of Zhanakorgan. Khorasan Ata lived in the IX century. Abd al-Jalil Bab Khorasan Ata is the fifth generation of Muhammad al-Hanafiya, the son of Ali ibn Abu Talib (Hazrat Ali), according to the genealogy of Nasab-nama. Khorasan Ata was a genius and healer who helped the Turkic peoples to embrace Islam.This shrine is unique in that it contains a replica of the Ka'bah in Mecca. Legend has it that Khorasan Ata flew to Mecca every Friday to pray, and his son Hussein said to his father, “If you allow me, I will copy the Ka'bah here in Mecca”. Khorasan Ata allowed his son to be tested. According to his son, he brought the Kaaba on the carpet. Believing in the power of his son, Khorasan Ata drew the shadow of the Ka'bah without putting it on the ground, and then a pile of sand was collected and the Ka'bah was built. The building was built for the purpose of training for pilgrimage and was used for this purpose. The entrance to the replica of the Ka'bah, made of clay as a local building material, is in the north-east. It is said that a worshiper who enters without praying on the floor, but prays in any direction in the four corners of the world, will be rewarded for praying in Mecca.

tolegetai-qylyshty-ata-kesheni.name: Tulegetay - Kylyshty Ata Complex
tolegetai-qylyshty-ata-kesheni.fact: Kyzylorda region is located about 30 km from the center of Zhanakorgan district.
tolegetai-qylyshty-ata-kesheni.lead: Kyzylorda region is located about 30 km from the center of Zhanakorgan district. Tulegetai Baba - a descendant of Kuchilik Khan. It is believed that he lived in the beginning of the XIII century.
tolegetai-qylyshty-ata-kesheni.bodyHtml:
Kyzylorda region is located about 30 km from the center of Zhanakorgan district. Tulegetai Baba - a descendant of Kuchilik Khan. It is believed that he lived in the beginning of the XIII century.When the Naimans were divided, Tulegetai was sent to the Uzgen-Turkestan region. Tulegetay and Kylyshty, who used to know each other's names in absentia, visit each other and respect each other. Tulegetay baba was a hero of his time, a figure who cared of the country`s destiny and thought about unity. In the Kazakh steppes Tulegetay batyr ruled the Naimans, who formed a separate ulys.The first person to write about Tolegetai Baba was Mukhametzhan Tynyshbayev, known to the peoples of Central Asia, who was the Prime Minister of the Turkestan Autonomy in the first years of the October Revolution. He said: “Tolegetai Suinishuli is a historical figure who lived in the XV century. Granddaughter of Naiman (from Naiman - Belgibai, from him - Suyunish, from him - Tolegetai). Tolegetai Baba was a hero of his time, a man who cared about the unity of the country”, - he said.According to popular legend, Kylyshty Ata was a saint with special qualities. Kylyshty Ata's father Kamaladdin came from Mecca and married the daughter of Ilgimagzum, a descendant of Abubakir Sydyk, the king of Kirzhent. Shortly afterwards, he returned to Mecca. When he grew up, the sword and the white horse came down from the sky and stood against 1001 plagues. When they came to the bis, the sword shone in the sunlight, and the fly that landed on the sword's face split in two. It means, “Anyone who is not honest can write like that”. From then on he became known as Kylyshty Ata. Kylyshty Ata is written in the books “Babyrnama”, Kamilkan Kattaev's “Makhdumi Agzam and Dagbed”, Sharafiddin Ali Azdi's “Zafarnama” about the life of Timur.

qorqyt-ata-memorialdy-kesheni.name: Memorial Complex "Korkyt Ata"
qorqyt-ata-memorialdy-kesheni.fact: The Memorial complex is 18 km from Zhosaly village of Karmakshy district of Kyzylorda region, at the bottom of Korkyt…
qorqyt-ata-memorialdy-kesheni.lead: The Memorial complex is 18 km from Zhosaly village of Karmakshy district of Kyzylorda region, at the bottom of Korkyt station. It is located one kilometer from the burial place of Korkyt Ata I.
qorqyt-ata-memorialdy-kesheni.bodyHtml:
The Memorial complex is 18 km from Zhosaly village of Karmakshy district of Kyzylorda region, at the bottom of Korkyt station. It is located one kilometer from the burial place of Korkyt Ata I. The memorial complex “Korkyt Ata” consists of several architectural structures: “hanging pipes” - the image of four kobyzs looking in all directions, the sound of the kobyz when the wind blows; “Pyramid of Wishes”, amphitheater, griffin and a ram, a museum, which forms an assembled image of a ram.The complex is dedicated to the great thinker, zhyrau, kobyz player Korkyt Ata, common to all Turkic peoples. Korkyt Ata is one of the saints of the Syr region. A written monument confirming the historical identity of Korkyt Ata is the “Book of Korkyt Ata” (“Kitabi dadam Korkud”). The Kipchak branch has a common heritage with the Turks of Oguz descent and the peoples of Azerbaijan. The Kazakh people recognize Korkyt as the ancestor of the kui. Korkyt Ata is portrayed as a zhyrau, a wise man, a genius, a leader, a shaman, a kuishi. Korkyt Ata is a great thinker of the Oguz-Kipchak tribes, a swamp abyss, a daulesker kuishi, a fortune teller who predicts the future. It is wise to watch over the survival of the people from external enemies and internal strife. He is an expert who always marks the migration of people, their place of residence, their brand, their motto. Korkyt is the owner of the flute, the grandfather of the kobyz. He left the wisdom that “in life there is death, there is change, there is no immortality, there is no unbreakable iron, everything dies, changes, is forgotten, only that which is immortal and unforgettable is the result of good deeds in human life”.

begim-ana-munarasy.bodyHtml:
It is located 35 km south of Zhanakurlys aul of Aral district of Kyzylorda region. It is a preserved architectural monument pf the X-XII centuries. Begim Ana Tower is a symbol of honesty and justice.The tower of Begim Ana is made of bricks and covered with square baked bricks. The tower is an octagonal prism-like dome, built in the form of a vertical pipe several times higher than the width.

A man who was in history, in the data of the XI century. is said to have lived. She is the daughter of Saint Karabura, who was both a hero and a believer in the Oguz-Kipchak period. Begim is the wife of Sanjar Sultan, the khan of the Seljuk state.It is known that the "Legend of Begim Ana" was widely spread and was the basis of many works and epics. Begim Ana Tower is not only a legend, but also the a unique architectural monument that tells the story.

zhankent-qalashygy.name: Zhankent Town
zhankent-qalashygy.fact: It is located 15 km from Orkendeu aul of Kazaly district of Kyzylorda region.
zhankent-qalashygy.lead: It is located 15 km from Orkendeu aul of Kazaly district of Kyzylorda region. Chronological period: VII-XIV centuries.One of the most famous cities of the Oguz tribes on the banks of the Syrdarya.
zhankent-qalashygy.bodyHtml:
It is located 15 km from Orkendeu aul of Kazaly district of Kyzylorda region. Chronological period: VII-XIV centuries.One of the most famous cities of the Oguz tribes on the banks of the Syrdarya. The city, which left its mark on the establishment of the Kazakh statehood. Zhankent (Yangikent - New City) is mentioned for the first time in the works of the Arab historian Ibn Rustem. The Arab geographer Ibn Haukal says that the main city of the Oguzs was Zhankent, which the Iranians called Nau-Kerde, the Arabs Al-Hariyat, and the Sarmatians Dahi Nau.The city flourished in the second half of the IX century and the first quarter of the XI century. The city of Zhankent was a city with an area of 15-20 hectares, where agriculture and trade flourished. The suburban irrigation system proves that agriculture was the mainstay of the economy. At that time, the Aral Sea was called the Ghent Sea. The people of Zhankent found a large source of salt near the sea and established trade relations with China, Iran and India.The city of Zhankent collapsed twice during its existence (1153,1219). begins to bloom again. A century later, Zhankent's hectic life came to an end. Zhankent is also popularly known as the city of snakes. The city of Zhankent is, most importantly, the basis for the formation of the Kazakh state, a prosperous center of Kazakh culture and art, a manifestation of trade and economic relations. The city of Zhankent was first built in 1867. Russian scientist P.I.Lerkh, studied in Soviet times S.P Tolstov.Zhankent is one of the sacred places along the Great Silk Road as a medieval city and the center of the Turkic peoples.

syganaq-qalashygy.bodyHtml:
It is located 10 km north-west of Tyumenaryk station of Zhanakorgan district of Kyzylorda region. Chronological period: VI-XVIII centuries.The first information about the city can be found in the X century Persian work "Hudud al-Alam". In the X century, Syganak was the trade and political center of the Huns and Kangly tribes, and in the second half of the XI century, the Kipchak state. During the Syganak, Deshti Kipchak was famous not only as a border trade point, but also for its vastness, safety and tranquility. Well-developed medicine.In its history of about 2000, the city was the capital of the Kanglys, the Kipchak Khanate (XI-XII centuries), the White Horde (XIII-XIV centuries), the Abulkhair Khanate (XV century), the Kazakh Khanate (XVI century). This city is important for the Kazakh people as a symbol of trade relations, economic relations between the states, the political system, tolerance, khanate, interethnic friendship and national identity.

zhent-qalashygy.bodyHtml:
Zhalagash district of Kyzylorda region is located on the right bank of the Zhanadarya River, 30 km south of the aul of Akyr. Chronological period: V-XVII centuries. It is a city that played a key role in the history of Khorezm-Oguz relations during the first upsurge of the Seljuk dynasty.According to written sources, the city was owned by the Oguz-Kipchak, in 1138-1152. It is written that it was under the rule of the Karakhanids. In the medieval work “Hudud al-Alam” it is shown as the city of Zhentiogyz. The city was conquered by the Mongols in 1220 and for some time was the home of Genghis Khan's eldest son Jochi.After the Mongol invasion, the city of Ghent was revived and became a major cultural and economic center in the Syr Darya region. There was a mint in the city and silver and copper coins were minted. Before the Mongol invasion, Ghent was a big city.The great researcher of the Syrdarya region, ethnographer SP Tolstov first showed the location of the city of Ghent in 1946, and according to the data collected from the surface, its age dates back to the XII-XVI centuries. concluded that. According to him, the XII-XIII centuries. Ghent was one of the cities of the Khorezm state

shirik-rabat-qalashygy.bodyHtml:
It is located about 100 km south of the aul of T.Komekbayev, Karmakshy district of Kyzylorda region, on the left bank of the old canal of Zhanadarya. The life of the city dates back to about IV-II centuries BCE - CE X-XII centuries.Chirik-Rabat is an outstanding monument of great historical value, preserved from the ancient Saka society of Kazakhstan. Due to the geographical location of the city, it was of strategic importance. It is located along the Silk Road, which connects Persia in the southwest, Russia in the south and China in the southeast. There were hundreds of ancient medieval cities along the Amu Darya and Syr Darya. The peoples living in the valleys between the two rivers cultivated crops by artificial irrigation, and cities and fortresses appeared. It is known that the city was a stronghold on the border of the Khiva Khanate and the Kazakhs during the policy of tsarist Russia in the XVIII-XIX centuries. In 1946, the Khorezm archeological and ethnographic expedition led by S.P.Tolstov discovered the city of Shirik-Rabat and explored it in 1948-49, 1958-59. It (120 km) is connected with the settlement of Sagdere. If we pay attention to the etymology of the word Shirik-Rabat, it is necessary to comment on the first word “Rabat”. The western and south-western sides of the fortress in Chirik-Rabat were densely populated. This is evidenced by the scattering of fragments of pottery and the remains of various products, ashes of fires.

shopan-ata-zherasty-meshiti.name: Shopan Ata Underground Mosque
shopan-ata-zherasty-meshiti.fact: Shopan Ata underground mosque is a sacred object in Kyzylsu (northern edge of Tuyesu sand), located 42 km northeast of…
shopan-ata-zherasty-meshiti.lead: Shopan Ata underground mosque is a sacred object in Kyzylsu (northern edge of Tuyesu sand), located 42 km northeast of Kyzylsai village. Monument to historical and architectural art of XII-XIII centuries.
shopan-ata-zherasty-meshiti.bodyHtml:
Shopan Ata underground mosque is a sacred object in Kyzylsu (northern edge of Tuyesu sand), located 42 km northeast of Kyzylsai village. Monument to historical and architectural art of XII-XIII centuries. He is closely associated with the name of Shopan Ata, one of the propagandists of Sufism. The mosque consists of 12 small rooms connected to each other. In front of the exit there is a cemetery with a curtain. It is said that Shopan Ata's daughter was buried there. There is a well at the bottom of the mosque.

According to legend, Shopan Ata was a disciple of the legendary Sufi Ahmed Yassavi, who followed the Hanafi school. One day, his teacher gathered his students and fired an arrow to preach Islam and Sufism to the world, explaining that they had to go where the arrow landed. Shopan Ata's arrow flew to Mangystau and fell into the hands of Bayan, a rich herdsman. Shopan Ata gets a job, but Bayan understands the purpose of his visit. The herdsman gives his daughter in marriage to Shopan Ata. Shopan Ata built an underground mosque at the foot of the mountain. Shopan Ata is known among the people as a spiritual nourisher who connected the religion of Tengriism and Islam.

qaraman-ata-zherasty-meshiti.name: Karaman Ata Underground Mosque
qaraman-ata-zherasty-meshiti.fact: Karaman Ata cemetery and underground mosque (XIII-XIX centuries), located 35 km south-west of Shetpe village…
qaraman-ata-zherasty-meshiti.lead: Karaman Ata cemetery and underground mosque (XIII-XIX centuries), located 35 km south-west of Shetpe village, Mangistau district, 5 km west of Kandybas winter pasture, is one of the oldest and largest cemeteries in Mangistau.
qaraman-ata-zherasty-meshiti.bodyHtml:
Karaman Ata cemetery and underground mosque (XIII-XIX centuries), located 35 km south-west of Shetpe village, Mangistau district, 5 km west of Kandybas winter pasture, is one of the oldest and largest cemeteries in Mangistau.

The cemetery includes medieval tombstones, stone fences, domes built in the second half of the XIX century and the beginning of the XX century by Adai masters, and many saganatams. In the western part of the cemetery there is an underground mosque Karaman Ata. The mosque consists of three rooms.According to legends, Karaman Ata, the son of Isan Ata, the son of Shopan Ata, had the same power in all respects as his grandfather. Karaman Ata cemetery and underground mosque were the places where Karaman Ata's oath of purity and honesty was held.

It was a place where the spear was aimed at each other, focusing on the difficult issues that led to the conflict and bloodshed between the country and the country, tribe and tribe. According to another legend, he came to Karaman Ata Mosque to take an oath in order to stop the long-running bloodshed between Turkmens and Adais. The Turkmens and Adais, who saw the power of Karaman Ata and Beket Ata, stopped the bloodshed and swore that there would be no more conflicts. Therefore, for the country, tribe and people, Karaman Ata Mosque was considered a powerful place that gathered, united and made friends of the country, tribe and people.

masat-ata-zherasty-meshiti.name: Masat Ata Underground Mosque
masat-ata-zherasty-meshiti.fact: It is located 15 km south-east of Ushtagan aul of Mangistau district of Mangistau region.
masat-ata-zherasty-meshiti.lead: It is located 15 km south-east of Ushtagan aul of Mangistau district of Mangistau region. Masat Ata cemetery and underground mosque date back to the X-XIX centuries.
masat-ata-zherasty-meshiti.bodyHtml:
It is located 15 km south-east of Ushtagan aul of Mangistau district of Mangistau region. Masat Ata cemetery and underground mosque date back to the X-XIX centuries. The interior of the mosque is like a four-winged house with a roof-like opening.

Masat Ata is a well-known figure who helped to establish Islam, a hero who defended his country from the enemy. He was famous among the men who carried out bloody campaigns against Kalmykia, defended his country from the enemy and fought hard. According to the legend, his enemies tried various ways to kill Masat Ata, but to no avail. It is said that when Masat Ata gets up for the morning prayer, his body's systems become loose and weak, and all around, the sand and stones melt. At that moment, the enemy came and killed Masat Ata. The beheaded man goes to prayer. Masat Ata ran out of the house with his head wrapped in a blanket, and a milk mare with a slave near the house followed. Traces of a saint, a slave and a mare, as well as traces of blood dripping from the neck of the grandfather fell on the greenery at the crossroads. The mare and the mare give birth. It is said that the hero, who died at the hands of a traitor, flew to heaven so as not to leave his body. But there are legends that the underground mosque remained in the same condition.

shaqpaq-ata-zherasty-meshiti.name: Shakpak Ata Underground Mosque
shaqpaq-ata-zherasty-meshiti.fact: Tupkaragan district of Mangistau region is located 40 km north-west of Taushyk village at the foot of Ongazy mountain…
shaqpaq-ata-zherasty-meshiti.lead: Tupkaragan district of Mangistau region is located 40 km north-west of Taushyk village at the foot of Ongazy mountain near Sarytas-Koshak bay. Shakpak Ata cemetery and underground mosque (IX-X centuries) are the most beautiful examples of mosques.
shaqpaq-ata-zherasty-meshiti.bodyHtml:
Tupkaragan district of Mangistau region is located 40 km north-west of Taushyk village at the foot of Ongazy mountain near Sarytas-Koshak bay. Shakpak Ata cemetery and underground mosque (IX-X centuries) are the most beautiful examples of mosques.

According to local sources, Shakpak Ata was a hero who had a deep knowledge of Islam, brought up disciples, taught children, and became famous in the war with the Kalmyks. The interior of the mosque, built in the form of an artificial cave inside the rock, is arranged like a fence through the central hall and faces north, south, west and east. According to Serikbol Kondybay's mythological research, Shakpak Ata is a devil who eats the dead and is the ruler of snakes. His real name as a historical figure is Shakhmardan, who is the grandson of Shopan Ata. It is called Shakpak Ata because in the battle with the enemy sparks came out of his weapon. According to the legend, when Shakpak-ata touched one of his nails when he needed fire, the sparks would scatter. He was revered by the people for his power to make fire out of stone and burn the rain with fire.Historian A. Medoev sufi suggests that he lived in the IX century, and V.V. Barthold states that Shakpak Ata lived during the reign of the Uzbek khan in 1312-1342 (XIV century).

of whole national importance. – Astana: Foliant, 2017. –233-234-pp.

It is located 30 km north-west of Taushyk aul of Tupkaragan district of Mangistau region, near Sarytas Bay. The cemetery of the Sultan Epe underground mosque dates back to the X-XIX centuries. According to research, the Sultan lived in the XIII-XIV centuries.

His real name is Kubbi, a disciple of Hodja Ahmed Yassavi, the son of Hakim Ata (Suleimen Bakyrgani).The mosque, carved out of stone, consists of several chamber parts. The Sultan's gorge and well are also noteworthy. The well, dug 6 meters from the cliff, has clean, cool and very tasty water. According to legend, the Sultan was a savior of mankind from floods. People begged, “Sultan, save me from the flood”. He raised the dead from the skin and bones.

sisem-ata-zherasty-meshiti.bodyHtml:
One of the largest and oldest cemeteries in Mangistau - Sisem Ata is located 35 km north of the village of Utes, Mangistau region, Mangistau region, along the winter wells and ancient caravan routes in the western Ustyurt.

Chronological period: XIII-XIX centuries.According to local legends, Sisem Ata was one of the first preachers of Islam in the medieval Oguz-Kipchak period. Sisem Ata's cemetery is a pantheon of heroes. Heroes who fought against the Khiva khans and other invaders are buried. Suyunkara batyr Orgeshbayevich, Tolep batyr Anetuli, Konai batyr Kenzheuly, Zhetimek Zhanuzak batyr, Kozhanasyr bai Zhanaiuli, Eskeldy Sanazar bai Kudainazarovich, Begei Daurdyl bai Kozybakuli, Sengir myrza Daurdurovich, Zharylgap bai Sengiruli, Seinet bienovich Tekenuli Esen The founders of the tribes Baiboz Bokkarauly, Nazar Zharyuly (Shotan batyr, Tastemir bai, Mailan, Kudaibergen), Zhanboz (Matai, Oteuli, Zhamankara), Zorbayuli Utegul, Karzhau Tulekeiuli and others. According to М. Mendikulov's research, the cemetery dates back to the XI-XII centuries, around the ancient part, on the tombs developed in a north-south direction, there are various symbols and traditional ornaments. The history of drawings refers to the political events of the Kipchak-Nogai epoch.

appaq-ishan-meshiti.name: Appak Ishan Mosque
appaq-ishan-meshiti.fact: Appak Ishan mosque in Shayan aul of Baidibek district of South Kazakhstan region is an architectural monument of the…
appaq-ishan-meshiti.lead: Appak Ishan mosque in Shayan aul of Baidibek district of South Kazakhstan region is an architectural monument of the late XIX century.
appaq-ishan-meshiti.bodyHtml:
Appak Ishan mosque in Shayan aul of Baidibek district of South Kazakhstan region is an architectural monument of the late XIX century. The mosque-madrasah was started by brothers Ishan from Turkestan - Kosym and Kulatay, continued by Kosym Ishan's son Seydakhmet and graduated by his grandson Appak Ishan. Maksum is the name that his father Seydakhmet called his son to call to prayer in the beginning. He was tall, thin, and handsome. He was always a pious man who did not wear white. Probably, that's why people called him Ak Ishan. When people heard about the opening of the mosque and madrasah, they began to flock. Since the small mosque needed spacious rooms for discipleship, King Seydakhmet obtained permission from the authorities to build a mosque-madrasah. The construction of three complexes of the mosque-madrasah took several years. The mosque, the auditorium, and the cells were built separately from each other and all in one square. No wooden materials were used in the construction of the mosque-madrasah. The domes are made of European-baked ceramics. The mosque and the porch are separated by arches - arches - 35 domes. These domes served as amplifiers at the time. The domes are high and stepped, no matter which way you look at them. The main dome looks special from afar. Appak Ishan mosque-madrasah in Shayan was once one of the largest educational institutions in Kazakhstan.

Reference: Kazakhstan sacred objects
of whole national importance. – Astana: Foliant, 2017. –288-290-p.

qarabura-kesenesi.lead: Karabura mausoleum is located in the central part of Suzak aul, Suzak district, South Kazakhstan region.
qarabura-kesenesi.bodyHtml:
Karabura mausoleum is located in the central part of Suzak aul, Suzak district, South Kazakhstan region.According to oral legends, Karabura was a religious figure and saint of the Oguz-Kipchak period, who lived in the XI-XII centuries. He came from the Tama clan of the Junior Zhuz. He lived along the Shu, Talas, Syrdarya, Volga and Ural rivers. Karabura helped to establish Islam and its beliefs without violating the traditions of the Saharan people. He expressed interest in the great representative of Sufism, Hodja Ahmed Yassavi. The spirit of Karabura is revered by the Turkic people. His mausoleum in Suzak has become a sacred place for the peoples of Central Asia.

ibrahim-ata-kesenesi.name: Mausoleum of Ibrahim Ata
ibrahim-ata-kesenesi.fact: It is located on the north-western edge of the aul of Sairam, South Kazakhstan region, on a high hill along the road…
ibrahim-ata-kesenesi.lead: It is located on the north-western edge of the aul of Sairam, South Kazakhstan region, on a high hill along the road to the village of Aksu.The dome was built over the tomb of Ibrahim Ata, the father of Khoja Ahmed Yassavi, a man known in the South Kazakhstan region for his Sufi teachings, priesthood and shamanism.
ibrahim-ata-kesenesi.bodyHtml:
It is located on the north-western edge of the aul of Sairam, South Kazakhstan region, on a high hill along the road to the village of Aksu.The dome was built over the tomb of Ibrahim Ata, the father of Khoja Ahmed Yassavi, a man known in the South Kazakhstan region for his Sufi teachings, priesthood and shamanism. Ibrahim Ata, a religious leader and a well-known preacher in the area, came from a noble family and was a successful farmer. Ibrahim lived a pious life, helping people in need. The mausoleum was originally built in the XVI-XVII centuries, but after its collapse it was rebuilt in the XIX century. The dome of the mausoleum collapsed and was rebuilt during a strong earthquake in the 1950s. The mausoleum was built of burnt bricks and partially plastered. It was whitewashed, rebuilt and repaired several times. After the demolition of the original dome, in the early twentieth century it was replaced by a sheet metal roof on all four sides, with a pig dome in the middle. The building has two floors with one location. There is an entrance on the south side and a window with a wooden frame on the west side. In the north-western and south-western parts of the mausoleum there are portals with shallow pointed cubes. The mausoleum of Ibrahim Ata, which is an architectural monument of culture and history of Kazakhstan, built of burnt brick, is a unique work of architecture.According to sources, Ibrahim Ata was the first leader of the Sufi community, founded in Yassi in the XII century.

Reference: Kazakhstan sacred objects
of whole national importance. – Astana: Foliant, 2017. –184-186 pp.

qarashash-ana-kesenesi.name: Mausoleum of Karashash Ana
qarashash-ana-kesenesi.fact: It is located in the central part of the Sairam residential area in Shymkent, South Kazakhstan region.
qarashash-ana-kesenesi.lead: It is located in the central part of the Sairam residential area in Shymkent, South Kazakhstan region. Karashash ana `s real name was Aisha Bibi, the daughter of the famous Sairam Musa Sheikh.
qarashash-ana-kesenesi.bodyHtml:
It is located in the central part of the Sairam residential area in Shymkent, South Kazakhstan region. Karashash ana `s real name was Aisha Bibi, the daughter of the famous Sairam Musa Sheikh. In the XI century, when Aisha Bibi lived, science, art and culture developed in our region. According to legends, Karashash ana could cure the disease and interpret dreams. Due to this, he became very popular among the population of the region. She paid a lot of attention to the upbringing of children. He knew the basics of Islam, the Qur'an by heart and was able to spread it among the people. Due to Aisha's behavior, people called her “Karashash ana”. Karashash ana mausoleum is a portal-dome construction. The mausoleum is dedicated to the mother of Hodja Ahmed Yassavi, Karashash. Originally built in the XIII century, it was later destroyed and rebuilt several times under the influence of time and natural conditions. The mausoleum is built of rectangular baked bricks. The modern mausoleum dates back to the middle of XIX century. In 1996, the dome is covered with white, and the southern and south-western facades are decorated with portals with elongated cubes. The front planes are shallowly trimmed and decorated with rectangular cubes. There are entrance doors on the south and west sides of the mausoleum. The end of the dome is plastered on the inside, the light hole above the entrance is covered with a wooden lattice. The floors are made of brick.

Reference: Kazakhstan sacred objects
of whole national importance. – Astana: Foliant, 2017. –186-188 pp.

baidibek-bi-kesenesi.name: Baydibek Bi Mausoleum
baidibek-bi-kesenesi.fact: It is located in Baidibek Ata aul of Baidibek district of South Kazakhstan region.
baidibek-bi-kesenesi.lead: It is located in Baidibek Ata aul of Baidibek district of South Kazakhstan region. Baidibek Bi Mausoleum was rebuilt in 1996 on the high bank of the Balabogen River in a new style, replacing the dome of the ancient tomb, preserved in the style of the Karakhanid era.
baidibek-bi-kesenesi.bodyHtml:
It is located in Baidibek Ata aul of Baidibek district of South Kazakhstan region. Baidibek Bi Mausoleum was rebuilt in 1996 on the high bank of the Balabogen River in a new style, replacing the dome of the ancient tomb, preserved in the style of the Karakhanid era.Baidibek Karashauly (about 1356-1419) was a leader of nomadic tribes in the Semirechye basin. According to his descendants, he was born in Tashkent. He lived in the Karatau region. He is a historical figure who inspired the country with his intelligence and heroic deeds. In his time, he was a great historical figure who united the nomadic nation and organized and initiated the defense of the country and the land from external enemy aggression, as a wise man, a commander. Old words in the country - according to steppe oral historiography, the Albanian, Suan, Saryuysyn, Shaprashty, Isty, Oshagy tribes, which are part of the Uisun association of the Great Zhuz, consider Baidibek as their ancestor. Baidibek Bi settled the vast Semirechye, the fertile plains of the Arys River, the Karatau and Tashkent basins, helped to unite the tribes, to unite them into a great zhuz, to unite them as a nation. The legends preserved in the country and the writings of the famous Orientalist, ethnographer Nikolai Aristov and Chokan Valikhanov are told.

Reference: Kazakhstan sacred objects
of whole national importance. – Astana: Foliant, 2017. –191-192 pp.

domalaq-ana-kesenesi.name: Mausoleum of Domalak Ana
domalaq-ana-kesenesi.fact: South Kazakhstan region is located on the southern slopes of the Karatau in the valley of the river Balabogen.
domalaq-ana-kesenesi.lead: South Kazakhstan region is located on the southern slopes of the Karatau in the valley of the river Balabogen. The mausoleum has been rebuilt several times and is still in its original form.
domalaq-ana-kesenesi.bodyHtml:
South Kazakhstan region is located on the southern slopes of the Karatau in the valley of the river Balabogen. The mausoleum has been rebuilt several times and is still in its original form. The mausoleum was overhauled in 1996 according to the project of architect S. Toktamysh.The mausoleum was built at the grave of Domalak Ana (real name Nurila).Domalak (Nurila) is the granddaughter of Maktym Agzam Khoja from Turkestan. He was born in 1378 in Turkestan. At the behest of her grandfather Maktym Agzam, Domalak ana married Baidibek bi at the age of nineteen (1397). According to local sources, she was nicknamed “Dihnat Ana” by a man of Turkish origin, Kara Haidar. “Dihnat mama” is a Persian word. In the Kazakh language it means “Holy Ana”. Over time, the word "Dihnat mama" underwent sound changes and became “round mother”. All his descendants were distinguished by their knowledge and wisdom and ruled the country.According to the legend, there are two sacred stones in the Domalak Ana mausoleum, among which only a pious person can pass. This dome-cemetery has become a special place of pilgrimage in the country.

Reference: Kazakhstan sacred objects
of whole national importance. – Astana: Foliant, 2017. –193-196 pp.

baba-tukti-shashty-aziz-kesenesi.name: Mausoleum of Baba Tukty Aziz
baba-tukti-shashty-aziz-kesenesi.fact: It is located in Zhylybulak near Kumkent aul of Suzak district of South Kazakhstan region.Baba Tukty Shashty Aziz is a…
baba-tukti-shashty-aziz-kesenesi.lead: It is located in Zhylybulak near Kumkent aul of Suzak district of South Kazakhstan region.Baba Tukty Shashty Aziz is a popular folklore and mythological figure in Kazakh folklore, a great hero.
baba-tukti-shashty-aziz-kesenesi.bodyHtml:
It is located in Zhylybulak near Kumkent aul of Suzak district of South Kazakhstan region.Baba Tukty Shashty Aziz is a popular folklore and mythological figure in Kazakh folklore, a great hero. At first, shamans who believed in the Blue God in the Sahara worshiped him as a ghost and later as a saint among Muslims.The mausoleum in the cemetery of the saint is made of burnt bricks. The mausoleum has a portal-dome, single-chamber construction. The quadrangle is surrounded by a convex dome mounted on a round neck. The façade is flat, unadorned, shallow and sloping, with an entrance in the middle, a small embossed tower on the double threshold. In the internal structure of the square house there are arches along the core, the dome rests on this arched roof. In the center of the mausoleum there is a brick tombstone. Baba marries a hairy haired saint. When she broke her contract, the fairy said, “You have a six-month-old baby. I will leave him in a place called Kumkent, look for him! ” flies into the sky. Baba came to the place where the hairy Aziz fairy told, found a baby in a coffin and named him "Edige".

of whole national importance. – Astana: Foliant, 2017. –177-179 pp.

ukash-ata-kesenesi.name: The Mausoleum of Ukash Ata
ukash-ata-kesenesi.fact: South Kazakhstan region is located 35 km north of Turkestan in the north of Babaykorgan rural district.
ukash-ata-kesenesi.lead: South Kazakhstan region is located 35 km north of Turkestan in the north of Babaykorgan rural district. Chronological period: IX-X centuries.
ukash-ata-kesenesi.bodyHtml:
South Kazakhstan region is located 35 km north of Turkestan in the north of Babaykorgan rural district. Chronological period: IX-X centuries.

Ukash Sahaba is a historical figure who first brought Islam to our steppes. There are many legends about "Ukash Ata". He is also called Ukasha Ata. The Companion of the Prophet Muhammad (peace and blessings of Allaah be upon him), a descendant of the last Prophet, was widely regarded as the military commander of the Muslims. According to the legend, Ukash Ata was a giant hero, impenetrable to swords and bullets. Anes, who lives at the beginning of the Kazakh genealogy, lives alongside the Companions. In addition to being a companion of the Prophet, Ukash Ata has valuable information about his ancestry. It shows that he is of Turkic origin.

It is believed that the water from the sacred well is connected underground to the Zamzam spring in Mecca. Priesthood purifies the soul, while white springs satisfy the thirst and purify the body. At the head of Ukash Ata well there is a small yurt-like structure. The depth of the well is 22-25 m. At the head of this well, the whole Muslim community comes to the shrine to pray to Allah and get rid of their sins. Everyone who comes here enters the mausoleum where the tomb of the first Ukash Ata is located and reads the Koran. Then he goes to a well at the top of the mountain to get water. The legend of the mausoleum, where the miraculous well and the tomb of the Companion lay, was widely spread in the past through songs and epics.

Reference: Kazakhstan sacred objects
of whole national importance. – Astana: Foliant, 2017. –164-166 pp.

sairam-qalashygy.name: Sayram Town
sairam-qalashygy.fact: It is located in the south-west of the center of Sairam district of South Kazakhstan region, 12 km from Shymkent.
sairam-qalashygy.lead: It is located in the south-west of the center of Sairam district of South Kazakhstan region, 12 km from Shymkent.
sairam-qalashygy.bodyHtml:
It is located in the south-west of the center of Sairam district of South Kazakhstan region, 12 km from Shymkent. Chronological period: VII-XVII centuries.Isfidjab is the historical name of Sairam, the place where the umbilical cord blood of Gulama Hodja Ahmed Yassavi was shed. Isfidzhab district included the cities of Keder, Syganak, Sauran and Yangikent on the Syrdarya and the cities of Balaj and Berukey on the northern slopes of the Karatau, Taraz, Kulan, Mirki (Merke), Suyab in the Semirechye.

In the XV-XVIII centuries Sairam was a major center of trade and handicrafts. was.Ruzbikhan Isfahani, a historian of the XV and XVI centuries and author of Mehman name-i Bukhara, wrote: “The walls surrounding the main part of the city are so high that the hand of the conqueror cannot reach its walls so quickly that the Kazakhs can't even jump over it». The pit outside Sairam is also mentioned in Hafiz Tanysh's work describing the events of the late XVI century. Information about Sairam can be found in Mahmut Kashkari's Diwani Lugat At-Turk. It reads: "Sairam is the name of a white city called Isfidzhab." The town of Isfidzhab was founded in 1923 by P.P. Ivanov, in 1925 M.E. Masson, in 1947, N.Bernstam studied it.

There are many mausoleums inside the town. The oldest is the mausoleum of Malik Baba. Isfidzhab (Sairam) was an important strategic center that controlled not only trade routes, but also the crossings to the Central Asian possessions and to the south of the Kazakh steppe.

iassy-turkistan-kultobe-qalashygy.name: Yascy (Turkestan, Kultobe) Town

iassy-turkistan-kultobe-qalashygy.lead: The center of the South Kazakhstan region is located 170 km from Shymkent, in the center of Turkestan.
iassy-turkistan-kultobe-qalashygy.bodyHtml:
The center of the South Kazakhstan region is located 170 km from Shymkent, in the center of Turkestan.

Turkestan is one of the oldest cities in Kazakhstan with a history of 1500 years. Ancient names of Turkestan - Turkestan, Kultobe V-VI centuries. formed in the XVI-XVIII centuries. It became the capital of the Kazakh Khanate. The first information about it in Arabic inscriptions dates back to the IV-IX centuries. begins to meet under the name Shavgar. The Arab historian-geographer Al-Istahri ibn Kordaubeh al-Tanrazi wrote: “Ancient Shavgar lived until the XI century, and in the XI century. The city center has moved to Yasy”, - he said. In the Middle Ages, the town of Turkestan was in a period of rapid prosperity due to its convenient location on the trade route. In the XII century, the poet, thinker, a great representative of Sufism Hodja Ahmed Yassavi lived and died here. makes up. Archaeological excavations revealed that part of the town, which was connected to the mausoleum building from the north-east and was bounded by the walls of the fortress, was its center - the fortress.

In 2017, the city of Turkestan was declared the “Cultural Capital of the Turkic World”.

zhylagan-ata-bulagy-men-ungiri.name: Crying Father's Spring and Cave
zhylagan-ata-bulagy-men-ungiri.fact: Zhylagan Ata Cave is located about 80 km from Turkestan, on the Karatau ridge, north of the village of Abay, along the…
zhylagan-ata-bulagy-men-ungiri.lead: Zhylagan Ata Cave is located about 80 km from Turkestan, on the Karatau ridge, north of the village of Abay, along the river Zhylagan Ata. It was once formed by the fall of rocks.
zhylagan-ata-bulagy-men-ungiri.bodyHtml:
Zhylagan Ata Cave is located about 80 km from Turkestan, on the Karatau ridge, north of the village of Abay, along the river Zhylagan Ata. It was once formed by the fall of rocks. Down the gorge on the left bank of the river from a height of 10-12 m there is a hollow with a diameter of 15-18 cm. From time to time water gushes from this cavity.Today many people visit it.

The cave is like an ordinary waterfall. Unlike a waterfall, water does not always flow from the “Crying Father”, but only to the person who reads the Koran. Even though it flows to some people, it does not flow to others. The reason for this is that “the water of the saint flows to those who have good intentions, and the evil eye does not flow to a person,” the elders explain. If you walk along the cave, a rock will come up and water will drip from it. It is called “Tears of a crying grandfather”.A person who has tasted water wants to drink it again and again. But do not boil water in a bowl. Then the water immediately disappears from the source. Once geologists heard about the power of this cave from a distance and came to the head of Zhylagan Ata, saying that “it must be just a wave of the sea” and conducted research. It takes two months to find out where the water from the cave came from. But during this time, no water came out of the cave. The astonished researchers shook their heads and said, “This is indeed the power of the Almighty!” that is. On the right side of the cave there is a small mausoleum - oval. Legend has it that an unborn woman who spends the night in this sofa will have a baby.

Reference: Kazakhstan sacred objects
of whole national importance. – Astana: Foliant, 2017. –28-32 pp.

aqmeshit-ungiri.name: Akmeshit Cave
aqmeshit-ungiri.fact: Akmeshit Cave is located in Baidibek district of South Kazakhstan region, about 90 km from Shymkent.
aqmeshit-ungiri.lead: Akmeshit Cave is located in Baidibek district of South Kazakhstan region, about 90 km from Shymkent. The cave is a hollow formed in the layer of limestone.
aqmeshit-ungiri.bodyHtml:
Akmeshit Cave is located in Baidibek district of South Kazakhstan region, about 90 km from Shymkent. The cave is a hollow formed in the layer of limestone. From time to time water drips from the holes in the shell. From the inside, the rim looks like the roof of a yurt.

Inside the cave there is a crack about 7-8 meters long. So people work hard and pray to God. In one of the several legends associated with the Akmeshit cave: in this cave there was a large mosque, which was important for the people. There was no access to the mosque from the outside, no one knew where it was. At the beginning of the twentieth century, part of the dome collapsed and was replaced by a hole leading to the cave. People built stairs here, and pilgrims came and stayed there. There were four underground passages leading to the central dome. Due to changes in the earth's crust, underground roads were closed and remained underground for several years. Only in the early twentieth century, as a result of research, the dome was restored. Named Akmeshit, this cave attracts visitors with its unique mystical world.

This is a sacred place for those who ask for a child - a child, who accepts the intentions of those who come sincerely. It also removes the tongue, eyes, and forehead. Akmeshit cave is always brown and cold: it is hot on the ground, here it is about 17-19 degrees.

Reference: Kazakhstan sacred objects
of whole national importance. – Astana: Foliant, 2017. –32-35 pp.

rabiia-sultan-begim-kesenesi.fact: The mausoleum of Rabiya Sultan Begim is a monument of medieval architecture (XV century).
rabiia-sultan-begim-kesenesi.lead: The mausoleum of Rabiya Sultan Begim is a monument of medieval architecture (XV century). South-east of the mausoleum of Hodja Ahmed Yassavi, 60 m. It was specially built for Rabiya Sultan Beg, the granddaughter of Amir Temir, the daughter of Ulugbek, the wife of Abulkhair Khan, the mother of the famous khans Kokenshi and Suyunish.
rabiia-sultan-begim-kesenesi.bodyHtml:
The mausoleum of Rabiya Sultan Begim is a monument of medieval architecture (XV century). South-east of the mausoleum of Hodja Ahmed Yassavi, 60 m. It was specially built for Rabiya Sultan Beg, the granddaughter of Amir Temir, the daughter of Ulugbek, the wife of Abulkhair Khan, the mother of the famous khans Kokenshi and Suyunish. In the south-eastern part of the mausoleum there is an entrance to the underground cemetery. The cemetery is plastered and painted. There are wooden coffins covered with leather. In the coffin of Rabia Sultan Beg there is a line: “This is the son of the mighty Amir Temir Koregen, the daughter of the mighty, great Sultan Ulugbek Guragan, who rests in peace.Rabia Sultan Begim lived about 1430–1495. She grew up in Samarkand and received a comprehensive education. In 1451, Abu Said, the grandson of Amir Temir, sent Ulugbek's daughter Rabiya Sultan Begim for military assistance to Abulkhair Khan during the conquest of Samarkand. After living with Abulkhair for 16 years and dying in 1468, Abulkhair had two sons, Suyunish and Kishkene. Rabia was one of the few Muslim women to take part in public affairs during the reign of Sultan Begim. She is the mother of the famous nomadic khans. In 1495-1510, by order of her son Koshkinshi khan, a mausoleum was built on her burial place.

Reference: Kazakhstan sacred objects
of whole national importance. – Astana: Foliant, 2017. –209-p.

otpan-tau-tarihi-madeni-kesheni.fact: This complex is located at the highest point of the Western Karatau in Mangistau (altitude - 532 m), in the middle of…
otpan-tau-tarihi-madeni-kesheni.lead: This complex is located at the highest point of the Western Karatau in Mangistau (altitude - 532 m), in the middle of the aul Zhyngyldy and Tuschybek sanatorium on the highway Aktau-Taushyk-Shetpe.
otpan-tau-tarihi-madeni-kesheni.bodyHtml:
This complex is located at the highest point of the Western Karatau in Mangistau (altitude - 532 m), in the middle of the aul Zhyngyldy and Tuschybek sanatorium on the highway Aktau-Taushyk-Shetpe.

A 37-meter monument to Aday Batyr was erected at the top of the mountain, and in 2007 a historical and cultural complex “Otpan Tau” was opened for the hero.In ancient times, when the country was invaded by the enemy, Uran burned Uran at the top of Mount Otpan in order to gather the people of the vast Mangystau and protect their homeland.

The flames from the top of Mount Otpan can be seen on the far Ustyurt. The motto “Otpan mountain is the face of our land, Adai Ata mausoleum is the seal of our country” describes all the power of this place. Mount Otpan is a place where our heroes and bis come together, consult and make decisions that will determine the fate of the country. Here our ancestors gave alms for the welfare of the country, prayed for the health of their descendants and sent them on a long journey. In ancient times, people had shelters from the cold, shade from the heat, tents from the rain, and shelters from the wind and storms.The spiritual, historical and cultural complex “Aday Ata - Otpan Tau” consists of the following structures: Aksaray - Akorda of Aday Ata; Exposition exhibition hall on the theme “Mangystau and the Seven Peoples”, systematized information on the history and culture of the peoples and tribes living from the Stone Age to the present day; Mausoleum of Aday Ata; Monument to the Mother; Emblem of Aday Ata; The symbol of the Turkic peoples is the Kokbori monument; Uranium fire; square of heroes; Tu Tobe.

Reference: Kazakhstan sacred objects
of whole national importance. – Astana: Foliant, 2017. –54-55 pp.

ybyrai-altynsarin-kesenesi.name: The Mausoleum of Ibrai Altynsarin
ybyrai-altynsarin-kesenesi.fact: The mausoleum is located 7 km from Kostanay, the center of Kostanay region, on the right bank of the river Tobol.
ybyrai-altynsarin-kesenesi.lead: The mausoleum is located 7 km from Kostanay, the center of Kostanay region, on the right bank of the river Tobol. The tombstone was erected in 1960. In 1991, in honor of the 150th anniversary of I.
ybyrai-altynsarin-kesenesi.bodyHtml:
The mausoleum is located 7 km from Kostanay, the center of Kostanay region, on the right bank of the river Tobol. The tombstone was erected in 1960. In 1991, in honor of the 150th anniversary of I. Altynsarin, a 1.5-hectare mausoleum was built on the site of the old monument. The mausoleum has a portal and a dome. Ibrai (real name - Ibrahim) Altynsarin (1841-1889) - an outstanding educator, writer, ethnographer, folklorist, public figure. Ibrai Altynsarin left a deep mark on the history of the Kazakh Enlightenment and the formation of the national school. He wrote a textbook "Kazakh anthology", a didactic textbook "Primary textbook for teaching Russian to Kazakhs."I. Altynsarin was the first in our literature to lay the foundation of the prose genre. In his speeches, he called on the young disciples to be moral, kind and brotherly, to work honestly and justly, to be polite and patient, to be attentive and to acquire knowledge freely. From 1879 to 1883, he opened new schools in four districts of Turgai region - Turgai, Irgiz, Troitsk, Aktobe. He became a full member of the Russian Geographical Society in Orenburg.
